title: Bail Application (BNSS Section 480)
description: Regular bail application before the Sessions Court under Section 480 BNSS (formerly Section 439 CrPC). High Court / Sessions practice-pattern practitioner aid (not sealed HC certified form).
body:
# APPLICATION FOR REGULAR BAIL UNDER SECTION 480 BNSS (formerly Section 439 CrPC)

IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE AT [DISTRICT]

Bail Application No. ____ of [YEAR]

IN THE MATTER OF:
[ACCUSED NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], residing at [ADDRESS] — Applicant/Accused

VERSUS

State of [STATE] — Respondent

FIR No. [FIR NO.] dated [DATE], P.S. [POLICE STATION], under Sections [SECTIONS] of [BNS/IPC]

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Facts of the case.** [Concise statement of the allegations and the applicant's connection to them.]
2. **Grounds for bail.**
   a. The applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated; [explain].
   b. The investigation is complete / the charge-sheet has been filed; custodial interrogation is no longer required.
   c. The applicant has deep roots in society, [family/employment details], and there is no risk of flight.
   d. There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence or influencing witnesses; [explain].
   e. The alleged offence is triable by [COURT] and the maximum sentence is [TERM]; prolonged pre-trial detention would amount to punishment before trial.
3. **Undertakings.** The applicant undertakes to abide by all conditions the Hon'ble Court may impose, including attendance before the Investigating Officer / Court and cooperation with investigation, as this Hon'ble Court may direct upon grant. Sureties and bonds (if any) are to be furnished only after bail is granted.

PRAYER: It is therefore most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to release the applicant on bail in connection with FIR No. [FIR NO.], on such terms as this Hon'ble Court deems fit.

Place: [PLACE]
Date: [DATE]

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Counsel for the Applicant

**Drafting notes:**
- Section 480 BNSS corresponds to the former Section 439 CrPC; confirm whether the Sessions Court or High Court is the correct forum.
- State clearly whether the offence is bailable or non-bailable and meet any statutory bars (NDPS s.37, PMLA s.45, UAPA s.43D(5)) with the applicable twin-condition tests.
- Attach a certified copy of the FIR and, where filed, the charge-sheet, and state the current stage of investigation.
- Plead parity with any co-accused already granted bail and rely only on verified precedents.
- Do not schedule sureties in the application. After grant, prepare surety / bond papers as directed in the order.

title: Legal Notice for Recovery of Money
description: Demand notice before filing a civil suit or proceedings under Section 138 NI Act for dishonoured payment obligations.
body:
# LEGAL NOTICE

[ADVOCATE NAME], Advocate
[CHAMBER ADDRESS]

Ref. No. ____ Date: [DATE]

REGISTERED A.D. / EMAIL

To,
[NOTICEE NAME]
[NOTICEE ADDRESS]

Subject: Legal notice for recovery of Rs. [AMOUNT] with interest.

Sir/Madam,

Under instructions from and on behalf of my client, [CLIENT NAME], resident of [ADDRESS], I serve upon you the following notice:

1. [Statement of the transaction — invoice/loan/agreement with dates and amounts.]
2. Despite repeated requests and reminders dated [DATES], you have failed and neglected to pay the outstanding sum of Rs. [AMOUNT].
3. Your failure amounts to [breach of contract / dishonour of cheque no. [NO.] dated [DATE] drawn on [BANK]].

I therefore call upon you to pay my client Rs. [AMOUNT] together with interest at [RATE]% per annum from [DATE] within [15/30] days of receipt of this notice, failing which my client shall be constrained to initiate appropriate civil and/or criminal proceedings against you at your sole risk as to costs and consequences.

A copy of this notice is retained in my office for record.

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Advocate

**Drafting notes:**
- Verify the exact principal due, the interest rate/basis, and the contractual or statutory foundation for the demand.
- Address the notice to the correct legal entity at its registered/last known address and retain proof of dispatch (RPAD/courier/email).
- State a clear, reasonable compliance period (commonly 15 days) and the consequences of default.
- Check the Limitation Act period for the underlying claim so the notice does not prejudice it.
- Keep the office copy and dispatch records for use as evidence if litigation follows.

title: Writ Petition under Article 226
description: Skeleton writ petition before a High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
body:
# WRIT PETITION UNDER ARTICLE 226 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA

IN THE HIGH COURT OF [STATE] AT [BENCH]
(CIVIL/CRIMINAL WRIT JURISDICTION)

Writ Petition No. ____ of [YEAR]

[PETITIONER NAME] — Petitioner
VERSUS
[RESPONDENT(S)] — Respondents

PETITION UNDER ARTICLE 226 FOR ISSUANCE OF A WRIT OF [CERTIORARI/MANDAMUS/HABEAS CORPUS/PROHIBITION/QUO WARRANTO]

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Parties.** [Description of petitioner and respondents, including the State authority impugned.]
2. **Facts.** [Chronological statement of material facts with dates and annexure references.]
3. **Impugned action.** [The order/action challenged, with date and issuing authority.]
4. **Grounds.**
   A. The impugned action is violative of Articles [14/19/21] of the Constitution because [reason].
   B. The impugned action is without jurisdiction / in excess of authority because [reason].
   C. The impugned action is arbitrary, unreasonable, and disproportionate because [reason].
5. **No alternative remedy** — [explain why the alternative remedy is not efficacious], without prejudice to the settled position that alternative remedy is no bar where fundamental rights are violated.
6. **Limitation/delay.** The petition is within reasonable time; [explain any delay].

PRAYER: (a) issue a writ of [TYPE] quashing [IMPUGNED ORDER]; (b) [interim relief]; (c) such other relief as this Hon'ble Court deems fit.

[PLACE], [DATE]
[ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Petitioner

**Drafting notes:**
- Identify the correct respondents (State, authority, and any necessary/proper parties) with their official designations.
- Show that an alternative efficacious remedy has been exhausted, or explain why the writ is nonetheless maintainable.
- Plead the specific fundamental/legal right infringed and the precise writ (certiorari, mandamus, etc.) sought.
- Explain and justify any delay or laches and attach certified copies of the impugned order and all annexures.
- Seek interim relief separately with supporting grounds and balance of convenience.

title: Demand Letter (New York, Breach of Contract)
description: Pre-litigation demand letter for breach of contract under New York law.
body:
# DEMAND LETTER

[FIRM LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

VIA CERTIFIED MAIL AND EMAIL

[RECIPIENT NAME]
[RECIPIENT ADDRESS]

Re: Demand for cure of breach — [CONTRACT NAME] dated [DATE]

Dear [RECIPIENT]:

This firm represents [CLIENT NAME] in connection with the above-referenced agreement (the "Agreement").

1. **Background.** [Summary of the Agreement and the parties' obligations.]
2. **Breach.** You have materially breached Section [X] of the Agreement by [describe breach with dates].
3. **Damages.** As a direct result, our client has incurred damages of not less than $[AMOUNT], [itemize].
4. **Demand.** Demand is hereby made that, within [10/30] days of the date of this letter, you [cure the breach / pay $[AMOUNT]].

If you fail to comply, our client will pursue all available remedies, including litigation in the courts of the State of New York seeking damages, interest, and costs. This letter is written without prejudice to and with full reservation of all of our client's rights and remedies, none of which are waived.

Very truly yours,

[ATTORNEY NAME]

**Drafting notes:**
- Confirm the client's factual account and available documentary support before asserting any claim.
- Mark the letter appropriately ("without prejudice" for settlement discussions) and reserve all rights.
- Check the applicable New York statute of limitations for each claim so the demand is timely.
- State a specific dollar amount, deadline, and payment method; avoid threatening criminal action to collect a civil debt.
- Send via a traceable method and retain proof of delivery.

title: Memorandum of Understanding (Services)
description: MoU skeleton for a services engagement between two Indian entities.
body:
# MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING

This Memorandum of Understanding ("MoU") is made at [PLACE] on [DATE] between:

1. [PARTY A], a [entity type] having its registered office at [ADDRESS] ("Party A"); and
2. [PARTY B], a [entity type] having its registered office at [ADDRESS] ("Party B").

1. **Purpose.** [Objective of the collaboration.]
2. **Scope of services.** [Deliverables, milestones, and responsibilities of each party.]
3. **Term.** This MoU shall commence on [DATE] and remain in force until [DATE], unless terminated earlier under Clause 8.
4. **Consideration and payment.** [Fees, schedule, taxes, invoicing.]
5. **Confidentiality.** Each party shall keep confidential all non-public information received from the other and use it solely for the Purpose.
6. **Intellectual property.** [Ownership of pre-existing IP and work product.]
7. **Binding nature.** Except for Clauses 5, 6, 9, and 10, this MoU records intent and is not legally binding. [Adjust as instructed.]
8. **Termination.** Either party may terminate by [30] days' written notice.
9. **Governing law.** This MoU is governed by the laws of India; courts at [CITY] shall have exclusive jurisdiction.
10. **Dispute resolution.** [Arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — seat, language, number of arbitrators.]

IN WITNESS WHEREOF the parties have executed this MoU on the date first written above.

[SIGNATURE BLOCKS]

**Drafting notes:**
- Specify clearly whether the MoU is binding or non-binding to avoid unintended contractual obligations.
- Define scope, deliverables, timelines, and any exclusivity or confidentiality obligations precisely.
- Ensure proper stamping under the applicable State Stamp Act and correct execution/authority of signatories.
- Align the governing-law, jurisdiction, and dispute-resolution clauses and confirm the arbitration seat and rules.
- Include term, termination, and a mechanism to convert the MoU into a definitive agreement.

title: Bail Hearing Preparation Checklist
description: Procedural checklist for preparing a regular bail hearing before Sessions Court or High Court. High Court / Sessions practice-pattern practitioner aid (not sealed HC certified form).
body:
# Bail Hearing Preparation Checklist

- [ ] Obtain and review the FIR, remand papers, and case diary extracts available
- [ ] Confirm the exact sections invoked (BNS/IPC and special statutes) and whether the offence is bailable/non-bailable, cognizable, and its maximum punishment
- [ ] Check statutory bars (e.g., NDPS s.37, UAPA s.43D(5), PMLA s.45) and the twin-conditions caselaw applicable
- [ ] Verify stage of investigation: charge-sheet filed? custodial interrogation sought?
- [ ] Compile antecedents: prior cases, if any, with outcomes
- [ ] Prepare roots-in-society material: residence proof, employment, family dependents
- [ ] Draft application without surety schedules; list post-grant compliance checklist separately (passport / attendance / sureties only after order)
- [ ] Collect medical/age/parity grounds if applicable; identify co-accused already on bail
- [ ] Line up precedents on parity and delay (with verified citations)
- [ ] Prepare a one-page case summary for the court with dates chronology
- [ ] Keep surety documentation ready offline for use only after bail is granted

**Practical notes:**
- Tailor the argument to the offence category and any statutory bar; be ready to meet twin-condition tests head-on.
- Rely on verified citations only and re-check parity and delay precedents against the latest position.
- Keep surety documentation ready for post-grant compliance only; do not plead surety particulars in the application itself.
- Anticipate the prosecutor's objections (antecedents, tampering, flight risk) and prepare concise rebuttals.
- Carry a one-page chronology and the key custody dates for the court's ready reference.

title: Civil Suit Filing Checklist (CPC)
description: Checklist for instituting a civil suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
body:
# Civil Suit Filing Checklist

- [ ] Confirm cause of action, accrual date, and limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963
- [ ] Determine pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction; compute suit valuation and court fees
- [ ] Verify mandatory pre-suit steps: statutory notice (e.g., s.80 CPC for government), contractual escalation/mediation clauses, s.12A Commercial Courts Act pre-institution mediation where applicable
- [ ] Draft plaint with verification and supporting affidavit; number paragraphs and annexures
- [ ] Prepare vakalatnama, list of documents, and original + copies for each defendant
- [ ] Include interim relief application (Order 39 Rules 1-2) with specific irreparable-injury averments if needed
- [ ] Address arbitration clause risk (s.8 application by defendant) in strategy note
- [ ] Arrange process fee and speed-post/dasti summons as permitted
- [ ] Calendar first listing, written statement timeline (30/90/120 days), and document preservation
- [ ] Client sign-offs: facts verified, documents authentic, litigation-hold instructed

**Practical notes:**
- Confirm pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction and the correct court/forum before filing.
- Verify limitation for each cause of action and plead the date of accrual clearly.
- Ensure court-fee is correctly computed and paid and the plaint complies with Order VII CPC.
- Institute a litigation hold and confirm the authenticity of all documents relied upon.
- Diarise the written-statement timeline (30/90/120 days) and the first-listing date.

title: Motion Practice Checklist (NY Supreme Court)
description: Checklist for making or opposing a motion in New York Supreme Court under the CPLR.
body:
# NY Motion Practice Checklist

- [ ] Confirm the CPLR ground and standard (e.g., 3211 pre-answer dismissal vs 3212 summary judgment after joinder)
- [ ] Check court-specific rules: Commercial Division rules, individual justice part rules, page limits
- [ ] Calendar deadlines: notice of motion (CPLR 2214) 8/16-day service windows; summary judgment deadline (120 days post note of issue or shorter by order)
- [ ] Assemble papers: notice of motion, attorney affirmation, party affidavit(s) on personal knowledge, exhibits, memorandum of law, statement of material facts (Com. Div. Rule 19-a where applicable)
- [ ] Verify admissibility of each exhibit; certify translations and business records (CPLR 4518)
- [ ] E-file via NYSCEF with proper document types; request oral argument if strategic
- [ ] Confirm meet-and-confer/affirmation of good faith where required (e.g., discovery motions, 22 NYCRR 202.7)
- [ ] Prepare proposed order and, for opposition, a counter-statement of facts
- [ ] Serve with affidavit of service; diarize reply deadline and return date
- [ ] Post-decision: calendar 30-day appeal window from service of order with notice of entry

**Practical notes:**
- Confirm the applicable CPLR provisions and any court-specific rules (Uniform Rules, part rules) before filing.
- Verify the service method and timing and file the affidavit of service promptly.
- Calendar the return date, opposition, and reply deadlines with adequate lead time.
- Prepare a proposed order and, where opposing, a counter-statement of material facts.
- Diarise the 30-day appeal window from service of the order with notice of entry.

title: Company Due Diligence Checklist (Acquisition)
description: Legal due diligence checklist for acquiring an Indian private company.
body:
# Company Due Diligence Checklist

- [ ] Corporate records: COI, MoA/AoA, statutory registers, board/shareholder minutes for 3 years, MCA filings (AOC-4, MGT-7)
- [ ] Capitalization: cap table, share certificates, transfer forms, ESOP scheme and grants, any encumbrances on shares
- [ ] Material contracts: customer/supplier agreements, change-of-control and assignment clauses, exclusivity/non-compete obligations
- [ ] Financing: loan agreements, security documents, CHG-1 charge filings, guarantees, compliance certificates
- [ ] Litigation: pending suits, arbitrations, tax disputes, show-cause notices; contingent liability schedule
- [ ] Employment: standard contracts, PF/ESI/gratuity compliance, PoSH policy and ICC, key-person retention risk
- [ ] IP: registrations and applications, assignments from founders/employees/contractors, open-source usage policy
- [ ] Real property: title documents, lease deeds, registration and stamp duty adequacy
- [ ] Regulatory: sector licences, FEMA/FDI compliance for foreign holdings, data protection (DPDP Act) posture
- [ ] Tax: GST registrations and returns, income-tax assessments, TDS defaults
- [ ] Insurance: policies, coverage adequacy, claims history
- [ ] Red-flag report with materiality thresholds agreed with client

**Practical notes:**
- Agree the scope, materiality thresholds, and reporting format with the client at the outset.
- Cross-check public filings (MCA, GST, litigation portals) against management representations.
- Flag red flags with severity and recommended remediation or price/indemnity adjustments.
- Maintain a complete document index and an audit trail of items requested versus received.
- Coordinate with tax, IP, and employment specialists for domain-specific review.

title: Consumer Complaint (Consumer Protection Act, 2019)
description: Complaint before a District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
body:
# CONSUMER COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 35 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019

BEFORE THE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION AT [DISTRICT]

Complaint No. ____ of [YEAR]

[COMPLAINANT NAME], [ADDRESS] — Complainant
VERSUS
[OPPOSITE PARTY NAME], [ADDRESS] — Opposite Party

1. **The complainant is a consumer** within the meaning of Section 2(7): [purchase/service details, consideration paid, dates, invoice numbers].
2. **Deficiency/defect.** [Describe the defect in goods or deficiency in service with dates and supporting documents.]
3. **Cause of action** arose on [DATE] at [PLACE] when [event]; the complaint is within the two-year limitation under Section 69.
4. **Jurisdiction.** The value of goods/services and compensation claimed is Rs. [AMOUNT], within this Commission's pecuniary jurisdiction; the opposite party [resides/carries on business] within its territorial jurisdiction.
5. **Relief claimed:** (a) refund/replacement of Rs. [AMOUNT]; (b) compensation of Rs. [AMOUNT] for deficiency and mental agony; (c) litigation costs of Rs. [AMOUNT].

VERIFICATION: [Standard verification with place and date.]

Annexures: [List — invoice, correspondence, notice, affidavit.]

**Drafting notes:**
- Confirm the complaint is filed before the correct forum by pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction (District/State/National Commission).
- File within the two-year limitation from the date the cause of action arose, or seek condonation with reasons.
- Plead "deficiency in service" or "unfair trade practice" precisely with supporting invoices and correspondence.
- Quantify each head of relief (refund/replacement, compensation, costs) and support it with documents.
- Attach the mandatory affidavit and ensure proper verification with place and date.

title: Anticipatory Bail Application (BNSS Section 482)
description: Application for pre-arrest (anticipatory) bail under Section 482 BNSS (formerly Section 438 CrPC) before the Sessions Court or High Court. High Court / Sessions practice-pattern practitioner aid (not sealed HC certified form).
body:
# APPLICATION FOR ANTICIPATORY BAIL UNDER SECTION 482 BNSS

IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE / HIGH COURT OF [STATE] AT [PLACE]

Anticipatory Bail Application No. ____ of [YEAR]

IN THE MATTER OF:
[APPLICANT NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], residing at [ADDRESS] — Applicant/Accused

VERSUS

State of [STATE] (through P.S. [POLICE STATION]) — Respondent

FIR No. [FIR NO.] dated [DATE], under Sections [SECTIONS] of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (formerly IPC) [and special statute if any]

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Apprehension of arrest.** The applicant has reason to believe that he/she may be arrested in connection with the above FIR / a non-bailable accusation, and accordingly approaches this Hon'ble Court under Section 482 BNSS (formerly Section 438 CrPC).
2. **Facts of the case.** [Concise statement of the allegations and the applicant's connection, or lack thereof, to them.]
3. **Grounds for anticipatory bail.**
   a. The applicant has been falsely and maliciously implicated on account of [enmity/business dispute/civil dispute given a criminal colour]; [explain].
   b. The accusation appears to have been made with the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant.
   c. Custodial interrogation is not necessary; the applicant is willing to join and cooperate with the investigation as and when required.
   d. The applicant has deep roots in society — [family, residence, employment] — and there is no risk of flight or of absconding.
   e. There is no likelihood of the applicant tampering with evidence or influencing/threatening witnesses.
   f. The offence, even if taken at its highest, is punishable with [TERM] and does not warrant pre-trial incarceration.
4. **Undertaking.** The applicant undertakes to make himself/herself available for interrogation, not to leave India without leave of the Court, and to abide by all conditions under Section 482(2) BNSS.

PRAYER: It is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to direct that in the event of arrest in connection with FIR No. [FIR NO.], the applicant be released on anticipatory bail on such terms and conditions as this Hon'ble Court deems fit; and pass such other order as may be just.

Place: [PLACE]
Date: [DATE]

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Counsel for the Applicant

---
**Drafting notes:** Section 482 BNSS corresponds to the former Section 438 CrPC. State whether a bailable/non-bailable offence is involved and address statutory bars (e.g., NDPS s.37, PMLA s.45, POCSO exclusions, SC/ST Act s.18 where applicable). Emphasise willingness to cooperate — courts routinely impose the Sushila Aggarwal-type conditions. File a certified copy of the FIR and, if available, a status report reference. Consider praying for interim protection until the application is heard.

title: Quashing Petition (BNSS Section 528)
description: Petition to quash an FIR/criminal proceedings invoking the inherent powers of the High Court under Section 528 BNSS (formerly Section 482 CrPC).
body:
# PETITION UNDER SECTION 528 BNSS FOR QUASHING OF FIR / PROCEEDINGS

IN THE HIGH COURT OF [STATE] AT [BENCH]
(CRIMINAL MISCELLANEOUS JURISDICTION)

Criminal Misc. Petition No. ____ of [YEAR]

[PETITIONER NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], residing at [ADDRESS] — Petitioner/Accused

VERSUS

1. State of [STATE] (through P.S. [POLICE STATION]) — Respondent No. 1
2. [COMPLAINANT NAME], [ADDRESS] — Respondent No. 2

PETITION UNDER SECTION 528 BNSS FOR QUASHING OF FIR No. [FIR NO.] dated [DATE] under Sections [SECTIONS] BNS

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Nature of petition.** This petition invokes the inherent powers of this Hon'ble Court under Section 528 BNSS (formerly Section 482 CrPC) to secure the ends of justice and prevent abuse of process.
2. **Facts.** [Chronological narration with annexure references.]
3. **Grounds for quashing (guided by the Bhajan Lal categories).**
   A. The allegations, even if taken at face value and accepted in entirety, do not prima facie constitute the offence(s) alleged or make out any case against the petitioner.
   B. The FIR discloses a purely civil/contractual dispute given a criminal colour to exert pressure.
   C. The allegations are absurd and inherently improbable; no prudent person could conclude that there is sufficient ground to proceed.
   D. The proceedings are manifestly attended with mala fides and are instituted with an ulterior motive to wreak vengeance.
   E. The parties have amicably settled the dispute (for compoundable/private-nature offences) and continuation would be an exercise in futility. [Attach settlement/affidavit.]
4. **No prejudice.** Quashing will not prejudice any legitimate investigation and will save judicial time.

PRAYER: (a) quash FIR No. [FIR NO.] and all proceedings emanating therefrom qua the petitioner; (b) stay further proceedings/coercive steps during the pendency of this petition; (c) such other relief as this Hon'ble Court deems fit.

Place: [PLACE]
Date: [DATE]

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Counsel for the Petitioner

---
**Drafting notes:** Section 528 BNSS preserves the inherent powers formerly under Section 482 CrPC. Frame grounds around the well-settled Bhajan Lal categories without over-arguing merits, since the Court will not conduct a mini-trial. For settlement-based quashing, attach a joint compromise affidavit and address whether the offence is of a private nature (heinous/non-compoundable offences are treated more strictly). Enclose a certified copy of the FIR and any charge-sheet. Seek interim stay of coercive action.

title: Private Criminal Complaint (BNSS Section 223)
description: Private complaint to a Magistrate under Section 223 BNSS (formerly Section 200 CrPC) seeking cognizance of an offence.
body:
# PRIVATE COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 223 BNSS

IN THE COURT OF THE [JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS / METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE] AT [PLACE]

Complaint Case No. ____ of [YEAR]

[COMPLAINANT NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], residing at [ADDRESS] — Complainant

VERSUS

[ACCUSED NAME(S)], [ADDRESS(ES)] — Accused

COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 223 BNSS FOR OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS [SECTIONS] BNS

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Parties.** [Brief description of the complainant and each accused and their relationship/connection.]
2. **Facts constituting the offence.** [Detailed, date-wise narration of the incident(s) with place, manner, and role of each accused.]
3. **Ingredients of the offence.** The above facts satisfy the ingredients of Sections [SECTIONS] BNS in that [map facts to each ingredient].
4. **Jurisdiction.** This Hon'ble Court has territorial jurisdiction as the cause of action arose at [PLACE] within its local limits (Sections 197-205 BNSS).
5. **Prior notice/complaints.** [State any police complaint made, its outcome, and why the private complaint is being filed; attach copies.]
6. **Statutory compliance.** The complainant is being examined on oath, and a list of witnesses and documents is annexed. The proviso to Section 223 BNSS (formerly Section 200 CrPC) (opportunity of hearing to the accused before cognizance) is noted.

PRAYER: It is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to: (a) take cognizance of the offences; (b) record the statement of the complainant and witnesses under Section 223 BNSS; (c) issue process/summons to the accused under Section 227 BNSS; and (d) pass such other order as deemed fit.

VERIFICATION: Verified at [PLACE] on [DATE] that the contents of paragraphs [__] are true to my knowledge and paragraphs [__] are based on information believed to be true.

[COMPLAINANT SIGNATURE]
Through [ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Complainant

LIST OF WITNESSES: [Names and addresses]
LIST OF DOCUMENTS: [Enumerate]

---
**Drafting notes:** Section 223 BNSS replaces Section 200 CrPC. Note the new proviso requiring the Magistrate to give the accused an opportunity of being heard before taking cognizance, and the requirement (where the complaint is against a public servant for official acts) of a report. The complainant and witnesses must be examined on oath; prepare them accordingly. Attach a list of witnesses/documents and an affidavit. Consider whether a Section 175(3) BNSS direction to police for investigation is a better route before filing a full complaint.

title: Discharge Application (BNSS Section 250)
description: Application seeking discharge of the accused under Section 250 BNSS (formerly Section 227 CrPC) for want of sufficient grounds to proceed.
body:
# APPLICATION FOR DISCHARGE UNDER SECTION 250 BNSS

IN THE COURT OF THE [SESSIONS JUDGE / SPECIAL JUDGE] AT [PLACE]

Sessions Case No. ____ of [YEAR]

[ACCUSED NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], residing at [ADDRESS] — Accused/Applicant

VERSUS

State of [STATE] — Respondent

Arising out of FIR No. [FIR NO.], P.S. [POLICE STATION], under Sections [SECTIONS] BNS

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Stage.** The charge-sheet under Section 193 BNSS (formerly Section 173 CrPC) has been filed and the matter is fixed for consideration of charge. The accused files this application under Section 250 BNSS (formerly Section 227 CrPC).
2. **Standard.** The Court, upon considering the record and documents and hearing the parties, may discharge the accused if it considers that there is not sufficient ground for proceeding. At this stage the Court must sift and weigh the material only to find whether a prima facie case is made out, not to hold a mini-trial.
3. **Grounds for discharge.**
   a. Even accepting the prosecution material at its highest, no offence under Sections [SECTIONS] is made out against the applicant because [explain ingredient(s) missing].
   b. There is no material connecting the applicant to the alleged offence; [analyse statements/documents].
   c. The material relied upon is inherently improbable / legally inadmissible / suffers from [defect].
   d. Sanction/mandatory pre-conditions (if any) are absent, rendering cognizance bad.
4. **Reasoned analysis.** [Paragraph-wise analysis of the charge-sheet, witness statements (Section 180 BNSS), and documents demonstrating absence of a prima facie case against the applicant.]

PRAYER: It is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to discharge the applicant of all charges arising out of the said FIR/charge-sheet, and pass such other order as deemed fit.

Place: [PLACE]
Date: [DATE]

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Counsel for the Applicant

---
**Drafting notes:** Section 250 BNSS corresponds to Section 227 CrPC (sessions trials); the analogous provision for warrant trials is Section 262 BNSS (former Section 239). Keep arguments confined to the record — the Court presumes the material to be true and only asks whether a prima facie case exists. Point to the specific ingredient not satisfied rather than arguing appreciation of evidence. Note the new statutory timeline requiring discharge applications to be filed within 60 days from supply of the charge-sheet copies. Attach the relevant charge-sheet pages.

title: Criminal Appeal Memorandum (BNSS Section 415)
description: Memorandum of criminal appeal against conviction under Section 415 BNSS (formerly Section 374 CrPC).
body:
# MEMORANDUM OF CRIMINAL APPEAL UNDER SECTION 415 BNSS

IN THE HIGH COURT OF [STATE] AT [BENCH] / COURT OF SESSIONS AT [PLACE]

Criminal Appeal No. ____ of [YEAR]

[APPELLANT NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], [presently lodged at [PRISON] / on bail], residing at [ADDRESS] — Appellant

VERSUS

State of [STATE] — Respondent

APPEAL AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND ORDER OF CONVICTION DATED [DATE] AND SENTENCE DATED [DATE] PASSED BY [TRIAL COURT] IN [CASE NO.] CONVICTING THE APPELLANT UNDER SECTIONS [SECTIONS] BNS

The appellant respectfully submits this appeal on the following:

**GROUNDS OF APPEAL**

1. The learned Trial Court erred in law and on facts in convicting the appellant despite the prosecution having failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
2. The Trial Court failed to appreciate that the testimony of PW-[__] is unreliable, contradictory, and uncorroborated on material particulars.
3. The Trial Court wrongly relied upon [confession/recovery/circumstantial evidence] which was inadmissible / did not complete the chain of circumstances pointing exclusively to the guilt of the appellant.
4. The Trial Court ignored material contradictions and omissions amounting to contradictions under Section 148 BSA (formerly Section 145 Evidence Act).
5. The benefit of doubt, statutory presumptions, and the standard of proof were misapplied to the appellant's prejudice.
6. The sentence imposed is, in any event, excessive and disproportionate to the facts and the appellant's [age/antecedents/period already undergone].
7. [Additional grounds as advised — each urged without prejudice to the others.]

The appellant craves leave to add, alter, or amend the grounds at the time of hearing.

PRAYER: It is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to: (a) admit the appeal; (b) call for the trial court record; (c) suspend the sentence and release the appellant on bail during pendency (Section 430 BNSS); (d) set aside the impugned judgment and acquit the appellant / in the alternative reduce the sentence; and (e) pass such other order as deemed fit.

Place: [PLACE]
Date: [DATE]

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Counsel for the Appellant

---
**Drafting notes:** Section 415 BNSS governs appeals from convictions (former Section 374 CrPC). File within the limitation period (30 days to Sessions, 60/90 days to High Court depending on the court appealed from) with a condonation application if delayed. Enclose a certified copy of the impugned judgment and grounds numbered separately. Include a suspension-of-sentence-and-bail application under Section 430 BNSS. Keep grounds crisp and mutually independent; avoid arguing evidence in the memo body — that is for the written/oral submissions.

title: Application for Maintenance (BNSS Section 144)
description: Application for maintenance of wife, children, and parents under Section 144 BNSS (formerly Section 125 CrPC).
body:
# APPLICATION FOR MAINTENANCE UNDER SECTION 144 BNSS

IN THE COURT OF THE [JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS / FAMILY COURT] AT [PLACE]

Maintenance Case No. ____ of [YEAR]

[APPLICANT NAME] (wife/child/parent), residing at [ADDRESS] — Applicant

VERSUS

[RESPONDENT NAME], son of [FATHER'S NAME], residing at [ADDRESS] — Respondent

APPLICATION UNDER SECTION 144 BNSS FOR GRANT OF MAINTENANCE

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Relationship.** The applicant is the [wife/minor child/unable-to-maintain-self major child/parent] of the respondent, having married/being related on [DATE at PLACE]. [Attach proof — marriage certificate, birth certificate, etc.]
2. **Neglect/refusal to maintain.** The respondent, having sufficient means, has neglected and refused to maintain the applicant since [DATE]; [narrate circumstances, desertion, cruelty, or cessation of support].
3. **Applicant's inability to maintain herself/himself.** The applicant has no independent source of income sufficient to maintain herself/himself and the dependent children; [details].
4. **Respondent's means.** The respondent is employed as [OCCUPATION] earning approximately Rs. [AMOUNT] per month and owns [assets], and is therefore capable of paying maintenance. [Attach available proof.]
5. **Quantum sought.** Considering the status of the parties, cost of living, and needs of the applicant and children (education, medical, rent), a monthly maintenance of Rs. [AMOUNT] is just and reasonable.
6. **Interim maintenance.** Pending disposal, interim maintenance and litigation expenses may be granted (Section 144(2) BNSS (formerly Section 125 CrPC)).

PRAYER: It is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to: (a) direct the respondent to pay maintenance of Rs. [AMOUNT] per month from the date of application; (b) grant interim maintenance and litigation costs; and (c) pass such other order as deemed fit.

VERIFICATION: Verified at [PLACE] on [DATE].

[APPLICANT SIGNATURE]
Through [ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Applicant

---
**Drafting notes:** Section 144 BNSS corresponds to Section 125 CrPC and is a secular, summary remedy independent of personal-law maintenance. Plead sufficient means of the respondent and inability of the applicant to maintain herself/himself. Attach an income affidavit in the format prescribed by the Supreme Court in Rajnesh v. Neha (both parties file affidavits of assets, income and expenditure). Interim maintenance is routinely awarded; press for it. Maintenance ordinarily runs from the date of application. Note enforcement under Section 144(3) BNSS.

title: Cheque Dishonour Demand Notice (NI Act Section 138)
description: Statutory demand notice for a dishonoured cheque under the proviso to Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
body:
# STATUTORY NOTICE UNDER SECTION 138 OF THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT, 1881

[ADVOCATE NAME], Advocate
[CHAMBER ADDRESS]

Ref. No. ____ Date: [DATE]

BY REGISTERED POST A.D. / SPEED POST / EMAIL

To,
[DRAWER NAME]
[DRAWER ADDRESS]

Subject: Demand notice under Section 138 NI Act for dishonour of Cheque No. [CHEQUE NO.] dated [DATE] for Rs. [AMOUNT].

Sir/Madam,

Under instructions from and on behalf of my client, [PAYEE NAME], resident of [ADDRESS] ("my client"), I address you as follows:

1. In discharge of a legally enforceable debt/liability of Rs. [AMOUNT] arising out of [transaction — loan/goods supplied/services/agreement], you issued to my client Cheque No. [CHEQUE NO.] dated [DATE] for Rs. [AMOUNT] drawn on [BANK & BRANCH].
2. My client presented the said cheque for encashment through [BANK] on [DATE]. The cheque was returned dishonoured vide the bank's Return Memo dated [DATE] with the endorsement "[FUNDS INSUFFICIENT / ACCOUNT CLOSED / PAYMENT STOPPED / EXCEEDS ARRANGEMENT]". A copy of the return memo is available.
3. The dishonour establishes that you did not have sufficient funds / arrangement to honour the cheque, and you have thereby committed an offence under Section 138 NI Act.
4. I hereby call upon you, in terms of clause (b) of the proviso to Section 138, to pay to my client the sum of Rs. [AMOUNT] within FIFTEEN (15) DAYS of receipt of this notice.

TAKE NOTICE that if you fail to make the said payment within the statutory period, my client shall be constrained to institute a criminal complaint against you under Section 138 NI Act (punishable with imprisonment up to two years and/or fine up to twice the cheque amount), besides civil recovery proceedings, entirely at your risk as to costs and consequences.

A copy of this notice is retained in my office.

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Advocate

---
**Drafting notes:** The notice is the mandatory pre-condition under proviso (b) to Section 138. It must be issued within 30 days of receiving the bank's dishonour memo, and must demand the exact cheque amount. Keep proof of dispatch (registered post/AD, speed post tracking, or email delivery) — service is presumed on correct-address dispatch. The 15-day cure period runs from receipt; cause of action to file the complaint arises only after it lapses without payment. The complaint must then be filed within one month of the expiry of the 15-day period (Section 142).

title: Complaint under Section 138 NI Act (Cheque Dishonour)
description: Criminal complaint for dishonour of a cheque under Section 138 read with Section 142 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
body:
# COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 138 READ WITH SECTION 142 OF THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT, 1881

IN THE COURT OF THE [JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS / METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE] AT [PLACE]

Complaint Case No. ____ of [YEAR]

[COMPLAINANT NAME], [through its authorised representative [NAME] vide Board Resolution/Power of Attorney dated [DATE]], residing/registered at [ADDRESS] — Complainant

VERSUS

[ACCUSED NAME], son of [FATHER'S NAME], residing at [ADDRESS] [and, where a company, its directors/signatories under Section 141] — Accused

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Parties.** [Description of complainant and accused; if a company, plead who signed the cheque and role of each accused under Section 141.]
2. **Legally enforceable debt.** The accused was liable to pay the complainant Rs. [AMOUNT] towards [transaction with dates].
3. **Issuance of cheque.** In discharge of the said liability, the accused issued Cheque No. [CHEQUE NO.] dated [DATE] for Rs. [AMOUNT] drawn on [BANK & BRANCH].
4. **Dishonour.** The cheque, presented on [DATE], was returned unpaid on [DATE] with the endorsement "[REASON]" vide return memo (Annexure __).
5. **Statutory notice.** The complainant issued the statutory demand notice dated [DATE] (Annexure __) which was served on/deemed served on the accused on [DATE].
6. **Failure to pay.** Despite service, the accused failed to pay within 15 days, thereby committing the offence under Section 138.
7. **Jurisdiction.** This Court has jurisdiction as the complainant's bank branch where the cheque was delivered for collection is situated within its local limits (Section 142(2)(a)).
8. **Limitation.** The complaint is filed within one month of the cause of action (Section 142(1)(b)).

PRAYER: It is prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to: (a) take cognizance of the offence under Section 138; (b) issue process/summons to the accused; (c) try and convict the accused and award compensation up to twice the cheque amount under Section 138 read with Section 357 BNSS; and (d) pass such other order as deemed fit.

LIST OF DOCUMENTS: (1) Original cheque; (2) Bank return memo; (3) Copy of demand notice; (4) Postal receipts and tracking/acknowledgment; (5) Authority/Board resolution.

VERIFICATION: Verified at [PLACE] on [DATE].

[COMPLAINANT / AUTHORISED SIGNATORY]
Through [ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Complainant

---
**Drafting notes:** Plead all six ingredients of Section 138 precisely: debt, cheque, presentation within validity, dishonour, notice within 30 days, and failure to pay within 15 days. File within one month of the expiry of the 15-day cure period; a delay-condonation application is permissible for sufficient cause (proviso to Section 142(1)(b)). Territorial jurisdiction lies where the payee's collecting bank branch is located. For company accused, array the company and implead directors/signatories with specific Section 141 averments of their role. Attach originals for exhibiting and an authority document if the complainant is a company.

title: Writ of Habeas Corpus (Article 226)
description: Habeas corpus petition before a High Court under Article 226 challenging illegal detention.
body:
# WRIT PETITION (HABEAS CORPUS) UNDER ARTICLE 226 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA

IN THE HIGH COURT OF [STATE] AT [BENCH]
(CRIMINAL WRIT JURISDICTION)

Writ Petition (Crl.) No. ____ of [YEAR]

[PETITIONER NAME] (relationship to detenu, e.g., father/spouse/friend), residing at [ADDRESS] — Petitioner

VERSUS

1. State of [STATE] through the Secretary, Home Department — Respondent No. 1
2. [Superintendent of Police / Jail Superintendent / Detaining Authority] — Respondent No. 2
3. [Private respondent, if illegal custody by a private person] — Respondent No. 3

PETITION FOR ISSUANCE OF A WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Locus.** The petitioner is the [relationship] of [DETENU NAME] ("the detenu") and is competent to move this petition, the detenu being unable to do so.
2. **The detenu.** [Name, age, address, and last known whereabouts of the detenu.]
3. **Fact of detention.** The detenu was taken into custody / is being illegally detained by Respondent No. [__] on [DATE] at [PLACE] and has since not been produced before any competent court / not been released.
4. **Illegality of detention.**
   A. The detention is without authority of law and violates Articles 21 and 22 of the Constitution.
   B. The detenu was not produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours as mandated by Article 22(2) and Section 58 BNSS (formerly Section 57 CrPC).
   C. The grounds of detention were not communicated; the detenu was denied legal representation. [For preventive detention, plead non-supply of grounds/representation rights.]
   D. [Where custody is by a private party] the detenu is being confined against his/her will without lawful justification.
5. **Efforts made.** The petitioner approached [police/authorities] on [DATES] to trace/secure release of the detenu, without result. [Attach copies.]

PRAYER: It is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to: (a) issue a writ of habeas corpus directing the respondents to produce the detenu before this Hon'ble Court; (b) declare the detention illegal and set the detenu at liberty forthwith; (c) direct an inquiry into the illegal detention and award compensation; and (d) pass such other order as deemed fit.

Supported by the affidavit of the petitioner.

Place: [PLACE]
Date: [DATE]

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Counsel for the Petitioner

---
**Drafting notes:** Habeas corpus lies against both State and private illegal custody. Establish (i) the fact of detention and (ii) its illegality — the burden shifts to the detaining authority to justify. Cite Article 22 and Section 58 BNSS (production within 24 hours). Such petitions are heard with urgency; seek an early date and, if the detenu's whereabouts are unknown, a direction to produce the case diary/custody records. For preventive-detention statutes (e.g., NSA, COFEPOSA), focus on procedural safeguards — supply of grounds, right of representation, and Advisory Board reference. Support with a sworn affidavit.

title: Public Interest Litigation (Article 226)
description: Public interest litigation before a High Court under Article 226 for enforcement of public rights.
body:
# PUBLIC INTEREST LITIGATION UNDER ARTICLE 226 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA

IN THE HIGH COURT OF [STATE] AT [BENCH]
(PUBLIC INTEREST LITIGATION JURISDICTION)

PIL Writ Petition No. ____ of [YEAR]

[PETITIONER NAME/ORGANISATION], [description and public-spirited credentials], residing/registered at [ADDRESS] — Petitioner

VERSUS

1. State of [STATE] through the Chief Secretary — Respondent No. 1
2. [Concerned Department/Authority] — Respondent No. 2
3. [Other necessary respondents] — Respondent No. 3

PETITION IN PUBLIC INTEREST

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Nature of petition.** This petition is filed in public interest for the benefit of [affected class/community] who, due to [poverty/disability/ignorance/social disadvantage], are unable to approach this Hon'ble Court themselves.
2. **Credentials and bona fides of the petitioner.** [State the petitioner's public-interest track record; declare no personal gain, private motive, or oblique consideration; disclose source of funds for the litigation as required by PIL rules.]
3. **Facts.** [Detailed, documented account of the public grievance — e.g., environmental degradation, denial of public services, violation of rights of a class, non-implementation of welfare law.]
4. **Public rights/duties involved.** The impugned state of affairs violates Articles [14/21/other] and the respondents' statutory/constitutional duty under [law/scheme].
5. **Representations made.** The petitioner made representations dated [DATES] to Respondents [__], which have gone unanswered/been rejected. [Attach copies.]
6. **No personal interest / alternative remedy.** The petitioner has no personal interest; the reliefs sought are for the public at large, and no equally efficacious remedy exists.

PRAYER: It is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to: (a) issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondents to [perform the specified statutory/constitutional duty]; (b) constitute/direct a monitoring mechanism to ensure compliance; (c) grant interim directions to prevent continuing harm; and (d) pass such other order as deemed fit in the public interest.

Supported by affidavit and accompanied by the disclosures required under the High Court PIL Rules.

Place: [PLACE]
Date: [DATE]

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Counsel for the Petitioner

---
**Drafting notes:** Establish the petitioner's bona fides and public-spirited credentials up front — courts scrutinise PILs to weed out publicity/private-interest litigation. Comply with the High Court's PIL Rules (declarations regarding personal interest, source of funds, and prior representations). Frame reliefs as enforcement of public duty, typically by mandamus, and consider seeking a court-monitored mechanism. Attach representations made to authorities to show the petition is not premature. Avoid disputed questions of fact best suited to a trial.

title: Special Leave Petition (Civil) under Article 136
description: Special leave petition (civil) before the Supreme Court of India under Article 136 of the Constitution.
body:
# SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) UNDER ARTICLE 136 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
(CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION)

Special Leave Petition (Civil) No. ____ of [YEAR]

[PETITIONER NAME], [ADDRESS] — Petitioner

VERSUS

[RESPONDENT NAME], [ADDRESS] — Respondent

(Against the final judgment and order dated [DATE] passed by the High Court of [STATE] at [BENCH] in [CASE NO.])

TO THE HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF INDIA AND HIS COMPANION JUSTICES OF THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

The Special Leave Petition of the petitioner above-named

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **The petitioner** submits this petition seeking special leave to appeal against the impugned final judgment and order dated [DATE] (Annexure P-1) whereby the High Court [summarise the operative outcome].
2. **Questions of law.** The petition raises the following substantial questions of law of general/public importance requiring adjudication by this Hon'ble Court:
   (i) [Question 1]
   (ii) [Question 2]
3. **Declaration under Order XXI Rule 3 SCR, 2013.** The petitioner has not filed any other petition seeking leave to appeal against the impugned order. [Adjust if a review was filed.]
4. **Grounds.**
   A. The High Court erred in law in [ground], resulting in grave miscarriage of justice.
   B. The impugned judgment is contrary to binding precedent of this Hon'ble Court in [principle, without fabricating a pinpoint citation].
   C. The findings are perverse, being contrary to the record and based on no evidence / a misreading of evidence.
   D. The impugned judgment gives rise to a substantial question of law of general importance that ought to be settled by this Hon'ble Court.
5. **Limitation.** The petition is within the period of 90 days from the impugned judgment. [If delayed, an application for condonation of delay is filed.]
6. **Interim relief.** Grave and irreparable prejudice will be caused unless the operation of the impugned order is stayed.

PRAYER: It is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to: (a) grant special leave to appeal against the impugned judgment and order dated [DATE]; (b) stay the operation of the impugned order pending disposal; and (c) pass such other order as deemed fit.

Drawn and filed by [ADVOCATE-ON-RECORD NAME], Advocate-on-Record for the Petitioner

Place: New Delhi
Date: [DATE]

---
**Drafting notes:** Article 136 confers discretionary, extraordinary jurisdiction — frame the petition around substantial questions of law of general/public importance, not mere error correction. File within 90 days of the impugned judgment (60 days if against an order refusing to grant a certificate) through an Advocate-on-Record, with the mandatory declaration and a synopsis and list of dates. Attach a certified/true copy of the impugned judgment as Annexure P-1. Include a stay application. Do not cite fabricated case numbers — reference the settled principle instead. Ensure the SLP paperbook complies with the Supreme Court Rules, 2013 formatting.

title: Reply to Police Notice (BNSS Section 35(3))
description: Reply/representation to a notice of appearance issued to a person by police under Section 35(3) BNSS (formerly Section 41A CrPC).
body:
# REPLY TO NOTICE UNDER SECTION 35(3) BNSS

[ADVOCATE NAME], Advocate
[CHAMBER ADDRESS]

Ref. No. ____ Date: [DATE]

To,
The Station House Officer / Investigating Officer
P.S. [POLICE STATION], [DISTRICT]

Subject: Reply to Notice under Section 35(3) BNSS (formerly Section 41A CrPC) dated [DATE] in connection with FIR No. [FIR NO.] under Sections [SECTIONS] BNS.

Sir/Madam,

On behalf of my client, [CLIENT NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], resident of [ADDRESS], who is the noticee under the above-referenced notice, I submit as follows:

1. **Acknowledgment.** My client acknowledges receipt of the notice under Section 35(3) BNSS (formerly Section 41A CrPC) dated [DATE] directing appearance on [DATE] at [PLACE/TIME].
2. **Willingness to cooperate.** My client is law-abiding, has not committed any offence, and is fully willing to cooperate with the investigation. My client [will appear as directed / seeks an alternative date of [DATE] owing to [reason]].
3. **Assertion of rights.** My client is entitled to and asserts the protections that (a) arrest is not automatic and shall be made only if the conditions in Section 35(1) BNSS are satisfied and recorded in writing; and (b) my client is entitled to the presence of an advocate during interrogation as recognised by law.
4. **Documents/clarifications.** My client [encloses/undertakes to produce] the following documents relevant to the inquiry: [list]. My client denies the allegations to the extent they concern him/her and reserves the right to a detailed response.
5. **Reservation.** This reply is without prejudice to my client's rights and remedies, including the right to seek anticipatory bail and to challenge any illegal or coercive action.

My client requests that the interrogation be conducted at a reasonable hour, that a copy of the proceedings be furnished, and that the statutory safeguards be observed.

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Advocate for the Noticee

---
**Drafting notes:** Section 35(3) BNSS mirrors the former Section 41A CrPC notice of appearance where arrest is not immediately necessary. The reply should confirm cooperation while firmly asserting the Arnesh Kumar safeguards — arrest only where the Section 35(1) conditions are met and reasons recorded. Keep the tone cooperative but non-incriminating; do not make admissions. Advise the client to attend with an advocate, carry ID and relevant documents, and note the officer's name/time. Where arrest is genuinely apprehended despite compliance, parallel-file an anticipatory bail application under Section 482 BNSS.

title: Criminal Case First-Hearing Checklist
description: Preparation checklist for a defence counsel's first hearing in a criminal case under the BNSS framework.
body:
# Criminal Case First-Hearing Checklist

- [ ] Obtain and read the FIR, and identify all sections invoked (BNS and any special statute) with their bailable/cognizable status and maximum punishment
- [ ] Confirm the stage of the case: investigation, charge-sheet under Section 193 BNSS (formerly Section 173 CrPC) filed, or committal
- [ ] Verify whether the accused is in custody, on bail, or on notice under Section 35(3) BNSS, and calendar remand/bail dates
- [ ] Check supply of charge-sheet and documents to the accused (Section 230 BNSS) and note the 14-day supply timeline
- [ ] Assess arrest legality and Section 35(1)/Arnesh Kumar compliance; note any custodial-safeguard violations
- [ ] Evaluate statutory bail entitlements: default/statutory bail under Section 187(3) BNSS if charge-sheet not filed in time
- [ ] Identify applicable statutory bars to bail (NDPS s.37, PMLA s.45, UAPA s.43D(5)) and required conditions
- [ ] Review the case diary references available and note contradictions/omissions in witness statements (Section 180 BNSS)
- [ ] Confirm sanction/cognizance pre-conditions where the accused is a public servant or a special statute applies
- [ ] Prepare vakalatnama, appearance memo, and any exemption-from-personal-appearance application
- [ ] Draft bail/anticipatory bail or discharge strategy and diarise limitation for each remedy
- [ ] Advise the client on do's and don'ts, surety readiness, and preservation of evidence/electronic records
- [ ] Note timelines under the BNSS for framing of charge, and calendar the next date and required filings

**Practical notes:**
- Note that the police report under Section 193 BNSS corresponds to the former Section 173 CrPC.
- Verify supply of all documents to the accused and object promptly if any are withheld.
- Diarise BNSS timelines for framing of charge and the limitation for each interim remedy.
- Advise the client on conduct, surety readiness, and preservation of electronic evidence.
- Confirm custody status and prepare the next-date filing checklist.

title: Cross-Examination Preparation Checklist
description: Checklist for preparing the cross-examination of a witness in criminal or civil trials, aligned with the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
body:
# Cross-Examination Preparation Checklist

- [ ] Map the witness's examination-in-chief and prior statements (police statement under Section 180 BNSS (formerly Section 161 CrPC) / affidavit / documents) and tabulate every contradiction and omission
- [ ] Identify the precise facts the witness can and cannot prove, and which case-theory points require this witness's concessions
- [ ] Prepare confronting extracts of prior inconsistent statements for use under Section 148 BSA (formerly Section 145 Evidence Act), with page/line references
- [ ] List documents to be put to the witness and confirm their mode of proof and admissibility (including Section 63 BSA certificate for electronic records)
- [ ] Sequence questions from safe/agreed facts to contested facts; avoid open-ended "why" questions
- [ ] Frame closed, leading questions permissible in cross-examination under Section 146 BSA
- [ ] Prepare to test the witness on opportunity, capacity to observe, memory, bias, interest, and prior conduct (Sections 148-153 BSA on credit)
- [ ] Anticipate re-examination and avoid opening doors that allow rehabilitation of the witness
- [ ] Plan impeachment of credit only where it advances the case; avoid needless attacks that harden the witness
- [ ] Keep a fallback set of questions if the witness turns hostile, and note the procedure to declare and cross-examine a hostile witness
- [ ] Prepare the goal statement: the three to five admissions you must extract, and stop once obtained
- [ ] Have the trial court record, marked exhibits, and a chronology handy for quick reference during questioning

**Practical notes:**
- Note that a prior statement under Section 180 BNSS corresponds to the former Section 161 CrPC.
- Build the cross around three to five essential admissions and stop once they are secured.
- Tabulate every contradiction and omission against the record for quick impeachment.
- Keep marked exhibits and a chronology within reach during questioning.
- Prepare the procedure to declare and cross-examine a hostile witness if required.

title: Civil Plaint (CPC Order VII)
description: Plaint for a civil suit for recovery/declaration drafted under Order VII of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
body:
# PLAINT UNDER ORDER VII OF THE CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE, 1908

IN THE COURT OF THE [CIVIL JUDGE (SENIOR DIVISION)/DISTRICT JUDGE] AT [PLACE]

Civil Suit No. ____ of [YEAR]

[PLAINTIFF NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], residing at [ADDRESS] — Plaintiff

VERSUS

[DEFENDANT NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], residing at [ADDRESS] — Defendant

SUIT FOR [RECOVERY OF RS. [AMOUNT] / DECLARATION AND PERMANENT INJUNCTION / SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE]

The Plaintiff above-named most respectfully submits as under:

1. **Description of parties.** The Plaintiff is [description, occupation]. The Defendant is [description]. [State any representative capacity, guardianship, or authorisation.]

2. **Facts constituting the cause of action.** [Set out chronologically the transaction/agreement, dates, amounts, correspondence, and the acts or omissions of the Defendant giving rise to the claim. Refer to annexed documents by exhibit letters.]

3. **Cause of action.** The cause of action arose on [DATE] at [PLACE] when [event], and continued to arise on [subsequent dates].

4. **Jurisdiction.** This Hon'ble Court has territorial jurisdiction because [the defendant resides / carries on business / the cause of action wholly or in part arose] within its limits (Sections 16-20 CPC). The suit is valued at Rs. [AMOUNT] for the purposes of jurisdiction and court fees, on which ad valorem court fee of Rs. [AMOUNT] has been paid.

5. **Limitation.** The suit is within limitation prescribed by the Limitation Act, 1963, the period being [ARTICLE/YEARS] commencing on [DATE].

6. **Pre-institution requirements.** [Where the claim is a commercial dispute, pre-institution mediation under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 has been exhausted / is exempted as urgent interim relief is sought. Statutory notice under Section 80 CPC has been served where a government/public officer is a party.]

7. **Notice.** A legal notice dated [DATE] was served upon the Defendant calling upon [him/her/it] to [comply], which remains uncomplied.

8. **Relief.** The Plaintiff therefore prays that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to:
   a. pass a decree directing the Defendant to pay the Plaintiff Rs. [AMOUNT] with pendente lite and future interest at [RATE]% per annum;
   b. grant a decree of [declaration/permanent injunction] as [described];
   c. award costs of the suit; and
   d. grant such further relief as the nature of the case may require.

**VERIFICATION**

I, [PLAINTIFF NAME], the Plaintiff above-named, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to [N] are true to my personal knowledge and paragraphs [N] onwards are based on information believed to be true, and that nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at [PLACE] on this [DATE].

[PLAINTIFF SIGNATURE]

Through
[ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Plaintiff

**ANNEXURES:** [List documents relied upon under Order VII Rule 14 with a separate list of documents.]

## Drafting notes
- Plead all material facts (not evidence) and attach every document relied upon; documents not filed with the plaint require leave under Order VII Rule 14(3).
- Ensure correct valuation — under-valuation invites rejection under Order VII Rule 11. Pay deficit court fee promptly if raised.
- For commercial disputes, comply with Section 12A pre-institution mediation unless urgent interim relief is genuinely sought (Patil Automation, 2022).
- Verify the plaint and file an accompanying affidavit under Order VI Rule 15/15A.

title: Written Statement (CPC Order VIII)
description: Defendant's written statement with set-off/counter-claim under Order VIII of the CPC, 1908.
body:
# WRITTEN STATEMENT UNDER ORDER VIII OF THE CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE, 1908

IN THE COURT OF THE [CIVIL JUDGE] AT [PLACE]

Civil Suit No. ____ of [YEAR]

[PLAINTIFF NAME] — Plaintiff
VERSUS
[DEFENDANT NAME] — Defendant

WRITTEN STATEMENT ON BEHALF OF THE DEFENDANT

The Defendant above-named most respectfully submits as under:

**PRELIMINARY OBJECTIONS**

1. The suit is not maintainable in its present form and is liable to be dismissed because [cause of action not disclosed / barred by limitation / barred by Section 11 CPC res judicata / non-joinder of necessary parties / arbitration clause attracting Section 8].
2. The suit is barred by limitation, the cause of action, if any, having arisen on [DATE], beyond the [ARTICLE/YEARS] period under the Limitation Act, 1963.
3. The suit is undervalued and court fee paid is insufficient.

**PARAWISE REPLY**

4. That the contents of paragraph 1 of the plaint are [admitted/denied as stated]. [Respond specifically; general or evasive denial is deemed admission under Order VIII Rules 3-5.]
5. That the contents of paragraph 2 are denied. The true facts are [set out the Defendant's version]. The Plaintiff is put to strict proof of every allegation not expressly admitted.
6. [Continue parawise, admitting, denying, or explaining each averment of the plaint.]

**ADDITIONAL PLEAS (AFFIRMATIVE DEFENCES)**

7. [Plead affirmatively: discharge/payment, accord and satisfaction, estoppel, waiver, fraud, coercion, failure of consideration, etc., with material particulars as required by Order VI Rule 4.]

**SET-OFF / COUNTER-CLAIM (Order VIII Rules 6 and 6A)**

8. Without prejudice, the Defendant claims a set-off / counter-claim of Rs. [AMOUNT] on account of [facts constituting the counter-claim]. Requisite court fee of Rs. [AMOUNT] has been paid on the counter-claim, which is within limitation.

**PRAYER**

It is therefore prayed that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to (a) dismiss the suit with costs; and (b) decree the counter-claim of Rs. [AMOUNT] with interest and costs in favour of the Defendant.

**VERIFICATION**

I, [DEFENDANT NAME], do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to [N] are true to my knowledge and the rest are based on legal advice/records believed to be true.

Verified at [PLACE] on [DATE].

[DEFENDANT SIGNATURE]

Through [ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Defendant

## Drafting notes
- File within 30 days of service; the court may extend up to 90 days for recording reasons (120 days as an outer limit in commercial suits, which is mandatory — SCG Contracts, 2019).
- Deal with every material allegation specifically; anything not denied is deemed admitted (Order VIII Rule 5).
- A counter-claim must relate to a cause of action accruing before filing the written statement and requires payment of court fee like a plaint.
- Attach documents in the Defendant's possession with a list of documents; seek leave for later production.

title: Temporary Injunction Application (CPC Order XXXIX Rules 1-2)
description: Interlocutory application for temporary injunction under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 of the CPC.
body:
# APPLICATION FOR TEMPORARY INJUNCTION UNDER ORDER XXXIX RULES 1 AND 2 READ WITH SECTION 151 CPC

IN THE COURT OF THE [CIVIL JUDGE] AT [PLACE]

In Civil Suit No. ____ of [YEAR]

[PLAINTIFF/APPLICANT NAME] — Plaintiff/Applicant
VERSUS
[DEFENDANT NAME] — Defendant/Non-Applicant

APPLICATION FOR AD-INTERIM AND TEMPORARY INJUNCTION

The Applicant most respectfully submits:

1. The Applicant has filed the accompanying suit for [nature of relief], the contents whereof are not repeated for brevity and may be read as part of this application.

2. **Prima facie case.** The Applicant has a strong prima facie case in as much as [state the right and the threatened infringement, with reference to title documents/agreement/registration].

3. **Irreparable injury.** If the Defendant is not restrained, the Applicant will suffer irreparable injury that cannot be compensated in money because [explain — e.g., alienation of unique immovable property, destruction of subject matter, breach of confidentiality].

4. **Balance of convenience.** The balance of convenience lies wholly in favour of the Applicant and against the Defendant because [compare comparative hardship, status quo, conduct].

5. **Apprehended acts.** The Defendant is threatening to [alienate/transfer/construct/dispossess/dissipate] the suit property/subject matter, particulars whereof are [set out]. Unless restrained, the suit will be rendered infructuous.

6. **Conduct and clean hands.** The Applicant has approached this Hon'ble Court with clean hands and without delay, and undertakes to abide by any order of damages under Order XXXIX Rule 2 if the injunction is found to be wrongly obtained.

**PRAYER**

It is therefore prayed that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to:
   a. grant an ad-interim ex parte injunction restraining the Defendant, its agents and servants, from [specific act] pending disposal of this application;
   b. confirm the injunction until the final disposal of the suit;
   c. grant such other relief as deemed fit.

The application is supported by the affidavit of the Applicant.

[PLACE], [DATE]
[APPLICANT SIGNATURE]
Through [ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Applicant

**AFFIDAVIT IN SUPPORT**

I, [DEPONENT NAME], aged [AGE], do solemnly affirm that the facts stated in the application are true to my knowledge and belief, and I have not suppressed any material fact.

[DEPONENT SIGNATURE]

## Drafting notes
- The classic trinity must be pleaded and proved: prima facie case, irreparable injury, and balance of convenience (Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh).
- For ex parte injunctions, comply with Order XXXIX Rule 3 — record reasons for urgency and serve the order and papers on the opposite party immediately.
- Candour is essential; suppression of material facts is a ground to vacate the injunction.
- Consider offering an undertaking as to damages and, where property is involved, seek appointment of a receiver or status quo in the alternative.

title: Arbitration Invocation Notice (Section 21, A&C Act 1996)
description: Notice invoking arbitration and calling upon the other party to concur in appointment of arbitrator under Section 21 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
body:
# NOTICE INVOKING ARBITRATION UNDER SECTION 21 OF THE ARBITRATION AND CONCILIATION ACT, 1996

[ADVOCATE/COMPANY LETTERHEAD]

Ref. No. ____ Date: [DATE]

BY REGISTERED POST A.D. AND EMAIL

To,
[RESPONDENT NAME]
[RESPONDENT ADDRESS]

Subject: Invocation of arbitration under Clause [X] of the [AGREEMENT NAME] dated [DATE] and demand for concurrence in appointment of arbitrator.

Dear Sir/Madam,

Under instructions from and on behalf of my client, [CLAIMANT NAME], having its office at [ADDRESS] ("Claimant"), I address you as under:

1. **The Agreement.** The Claimant and you ("Respondent") entered into the [AGREEMENT NAME] dated [DATE] ("Agreement") for [purpose]. Clause [X] of the Agreement contains an arbitration agreement providing for reference of disputes to arbitration [seat: [CITY]; number of arbitrators: [ONE/THREE]; governing rules: [INSTITUTIONAL/ad hoc]; language: [LANGUAGE]].

2. **Disputes and differences.** Disputes have arisen between the parties in relation to [describe the disputes — non-payment/defective performance/wrongful termination, with dates and amounts]. Despite the Claimant's [notices/reminders] dated [DATES], the Respondent has failed to [comply].

3. **Claims.** The Claimant's claims include, without limitation: (a) Rs. [AMOUNT] towards [head]; (b) interest at [RATE]% per annum from [DATE] to realisation; (c) costs of the arbitration; and (d) such further reliefs as may be advised.

4. **Invocation.** The Claimant hereby invokes the arbitration agreement contained in Clause [X] and refers the aforesaid disputes to arbitration in accordance with the Act. This notice constitutes the commencement of arbitral proceedings under Section 21 of the Act with effect from the date of your receipt hereof.

5. **Appointment of arbitrator.** The Claimant proposes the name of [PROPOSED ARBITRATOR / that the sole arbitrator be appointed by mutual consent]. You are called upon to convey your concurrence to the proposed arbitrator, or to suggest an agreeable name, within thirty (30) days of receipt of this notice, failing which the Claimant shall be constrained to approach the Hon'ble [High Court/Supreme Court] under Section 11 of the Act for appointment of the arbitral tribunal, at your risk as to costs.

6. The proposed arbitrator's disclosure under Section 12 read with the Fifth and Seventh Schedules shall be obtained to ensure independence and impartiality.

This notice is without prejudice to the Claimant's rights and remedies, all of which are expressly reserved.

Yours faithfully,

[ADVOCATE NAME], Advocate
For and on behalf of [CLAIMANT NAME]

## Drafting notes
- A Section 21 notice is a mandatory precondition to a Section 11 application and fixes the date of commencement, which is relevant to limitation.
- Identify the disputes with reasonable particularity — vague invocation can be challenged.
- Respect the appointment mechanism in the clause; propose a neutral arbitrator and address independence under the Fifth/Seventh Schedules (a party cannot unilaterally appoint where ineligible — TRF Ltd/Perkins line of cases).
- Preserve limitation: the notice should be issued well within three years of the cause of action.

title: Statement of Claim (Arbitration)
description: Claimant's statement of claim before an arbitral tribunal under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
body:
# STATEMENT OF CLAIM

BEFORE THE [SOLE ARBITRATOR / ARBITRAL TRIBUNAL] APPOINTED UNDER CLAUSE [X] OF THE [AGREEMENT NAME] DATED [DATE]

Seat of Arbitration: [CITY]

IN THE MATTER OF ARBITRATION BETWEEN:
[CLAIMANT NAME], [ADDRESS] — Claimant
AND
[RESPONDENT NAME], [ADDRESS] — Respondent

STATEMENT OF CLAIM UNDER SECTION 23 OF THE ARBITRATION AND CONCILIATION ACT, 1996

**I. INTRODUCTION AND PARTIES**
1. The Claimant is [description]. The Respondent is [description]. The parties are governed by the Agreement dated [DATE].

**II. THE ARBITRATION AGREEMENT AND JURISDICTION**
2. Clause [X] of the Agreement constitutes a valid arbitration agreement. The Tribunal is duly constituted and has jurisdiction under Section 16 to determine the disputes referred herein. Arbitration was invoked by notice dated [DATE] under Section 21.

**III. FACTUAL BACKGROUND**
3. [Chronological narration of the contract, scope of work/supply, milestones, payments, correspondence, and the events giving rise to the dispute, with references to documents at Volume/Exhibit numbers.]

**IV. BREACHES BY THE RESPONDENT**
4. The Respondent committed the following breaches: [itemise each breach, the clause breached, and the consequences].

**V. CLAIMS AND QUANTIFICATION**
5. **Claim 1 — [head].** Rs. [AMOUNT], computed as [basis/formula].
6. **Claim 2 — [head].** Rs. [AMOUNT].
7. **Interest.** Pre-reference, pendente lite, and future interest at [RATE]% per annum under Section 31(7) of the Act.
8. **Costs.** Costs of the arbitration under Section 31A.

**VI. LIMITATION**
9. The claims are within limitation, arbitration having been invoked on [DATE], within three years of accrual of the cause of action.

**VII. RELIEFS SOUGHT**
The Claimant prays that the Tribunal be pleased to pass an award:
   a. directing the Respondent to pay the Claimant Rs. [TOTAL];
   b. awarding interest at [RATE]% per annum as aforesaid;
   c. awarding costs of the arbitration; and
   d. granting such further relief as the Tribunal deems fit.

**VERIFICATION AND STATEMENT OF TRUTH**
The Claimant affirms that the contents of this Statement of Claim are true and correct to its knowledge and belief. A list of documents and witness statement(s) accompany this Statement.

For [CLAIMANT NAME]
[AUTHORISED SIGNATORY] / [COUNSEL]
Date: [DATE]

## Drafting notes
- File within the timeline fixed by the Tribunal's Procedural Order No. 1; seek the Tribunal's directions on document production and witness statements early.
- Plead jurisdiction affirmatively and anticipate any Section 16 challenge.
- Quantify each claim head with a clear basis; annex a summary quantum table and supporting documents.
- Keep the reliefs precise to enable a clean, enforceable award and to minimise Section 34 challenge risk.

title: Section 9 IBC Demand Notice (Form 3)
description: Operational creditor's demand notice in Form 3 under Section 8 read with Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
body:
# DEMAND NOTICE UNDER SECTION 8 OF THE INSOLVENCY AND BANKRUPTCY CODE, 2016 (FORM 3)

[Rule 5(1)(a) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016]

BY REGISTERED POST A.D. / SPEED POST / EMAIL

Date: [DATE]

To,
The Directors / Registered Office,
[CORPORATE DEBTOR NAME]
[REGISTERED ADDRESS]

Subject: Demand notice / invoice demanding payment of unpaid operational debt of Rs. [AMOUNT] in respect of [GOODS/SERVICES].

1. This letter is a demand notice under Section 8 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 ("the Code") read with Rule 5 of the Adjudicating Authority Rules, calling upon [CORPORATE DEBTOR NAME] ("Corporate Debtor") to pay the unpaid operational debt set out below.

2. **Particulars of operational debt:**
   a. Total amount of debt, including interest: Rs. [AMOUNT].
   b. Amount in default: Rs. [AMOUNT].
   c. Date on which the debt fell due: [DATE].
   d. Date on which the default occurred: [DATE].
   e. Particulars of the transaction: [purchase orders, invoices numbered [NOS.] dated [DATES], service agreement dated [DATE]].
   f. Details of retention of title arrangements, if any: [NA / details].
   g. Record of default with an information utility, if any: [NA / details].
   h. Provision of law, contract, or other document under which the debt has become due: [invoice terms / agreement Clause [X] providing interest at [RATE]% per annum].

3. The Corporate Debtor is called upon to pay the aforesaid unpaid operational debt of Rs. [AMOUNT] in full within ten (10) days of the receipt of this notice, failing which the operational creditor shall initiate a corporate insolvency resolution process under Section 9 of the Code before the National Company Law Tribunal, [BENCH].

4. The Corporate Debtor is further put to notice that, if there exists any dispute or record of the pendency of a suit or arbitration proceeding in relation to such debt, the same must be brought to the notice of the operational creditor within ten (10) days of the receipt of this notice under Section 8(2) of the Code.

**Details of the operational creditor:**
Name: [OPERATIONAL CREDITOR NAME]
Address: [ADDRESS]
Person authorised to act: [NAME, DESIGNATION]
Contact / Email: [DETAILS]

[SIGNATURE]
[Name and position of person signing, with authorisation/board resolution reference]

**Instructions:** Please serve a copy of this notice on the corporate person at its registered office and retain proof of delivery.

## Drafting notes
- Use Form 3 where the demand is by way of a notice (Form 4 where a copy of the invoice demanding payment is attached). Ensure the threshold amount of default (currently Rs. 1 crore) is met.
- A pre-existing genuine dispute defeats a Section 9 application (Mobilox Innovations v. Kirusa) — assess correspondence before issuing.
- Attach proof of delivery; the ten-day period runs from receipt.
- Interest can be part of operational debt only if contractually or statutorily payable; plead the basis clearly.

title: Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (India)
description: Bilateral confidentiality agreement between two Indian parties exchanging confidential information.
body:
# MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement ("Agreement") is made at [PLACE] on [DATE] BETWEEN:

(1) [PARTY A NAME], a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 having its registered office at [ADDRESS] ("Party A"); and
(2) [PARTY B NAME], a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 having its registered office at [ADDRESS] ("Party B").

Party A and Party B are individually a "Party" and collectively the "Parties". Each Party may act as a "Disclosing Party" or "Receiving Party".

**WHEREAS** the Parties wish to explore a potential [business relationship/transaction] (the "Purpose") and, for that Purpose, may disclose to each other certain confidential information.

NOW THEREFORE the Parties agree:

1. **Definition of Confidential Information.** "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by the Disclosing Party, whether oral, written, electronic, or visual, including business plans, financials, customer data, technical data, source code, and trade secrets, whether or not marked "confidential".
