12. **Books and Records; Separateness.** The Company shall maintain separate books, bank accounts, and records, and shall observe formalities sufficient to preserve its limited-liability status.
13. **Amendment.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by the Member.
14. **Governing Law.** This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of [STATE].

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Member has executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

_____________________________
[MEMBER NAME], Member

## Drafting notes
Even for a single member, a written operating agreement helps preserve limited liability by evidencing that the LLC is a separate entity — reinforce this by maintaining separate accounts and avoiding commingling (the key to resisting veil-piercing). Confirm the governing-state Act's default rules and whether the state requires the operating agreement to be in writing. Address the tax election deliberately: single-member LLCs are disregarded by default, but an S-corp election (Form 2553) can reduce self-employment tax if eligibility and reasonable-compensation rules are met. Consider succession provisions (e.g., a designated successor member) since there is no other member.

title: Board Consent in Lieu of Meeting
description: Unanimous written consent of the board of directors in lieu of a meeting for corporate actions.
body:
# ACTION BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], INC.

In Lieu of a Meeting — [DATE]

The undersigned, being all of the members of the Board of Directors (the "Board") of [COMPANY NAME], Inc., a [STATE] corporation (the "Corporation"), acting pursuant to [Section [X] of the [STATE] General Corporation Law] and the Corporation's bylaws, hereby adopt the following resolutions by unanimous written consent without a meeting, effective as of the date set forth above.

## APPROVAL OF [SUBJECT]
WHEREAS, the Board has determined that it is in the best interests of the Corporation and its stockholders to [describe the action, e.g., authorize the issuance of shares / approve the appointment of an officer / approve a financing];

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT:

**RESOLVED**, that [the specific action is approved], on the terms and conditions described in [the materials presented to the Board / Exhibit A]; and

**RESOLVED FURTHER**, that the officers of the Corporation are, and each of them individually is, hereby authorized and directed to take all actions and execute and deliver all documents they deem necessary or advisable to carry out the intent and purpose of the foregoing resolution; and

**RESOLVED FURTHER**, that any actions taken by the officers of the Corporation prior to the date of these resolutions that are within the authority conferred hereby are ratified, confirmed, and approved in all respects.

## OMNIBUS RESOLUTION
**RESOLVED**, that all acts and things previously done by any director or officer of the Corporation in furtherance of the foregoing resolutions are hereby ratified and confirmed.

This consent may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which is deemed an original, and by electronic signature, and shall be filed with the minutes of the proceedings of the Board.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned have executed this Written Consent as of the date first written above.

_____________________________        _____________________________
[DIRECTOR NAME], Director            [DIRECTOR NAME], Director

## Drafting notes
Most state corporation statutes permit board action by written consent only if it is unanimous (unlike stockholder consents, which many states allow by majority) — confirm the governing statute and the bylaws, and obtain every director's signature. Recite the effective date clearly and attach supporting materials as exhibits when the action requires specific terms (share counts, purchase price, plan documents). File the executed consent in the minute book. For interested-director transactions, address the conflict under the applicable statute (e.g., DGCL § 144) with disclosure and disinterested approval.

title: Attorney Engagement Letter
description: Engagement letter establishing the attorney-client relationship, scope, and fee arrangement.
body:
# ENGAGEMENT LETTER

[FIRM LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

[CLIENT NAME]
[CLIENT ADDRESS]

Re: Engagement of [FIRM NAME] — [MATTER DESCRIPTION]

Dear [CLIENT NAME]:

Thank you for retaining [FIRM NAME] (the "Firm"). This letter sets forth the terms of our engagement.

1. **Scope of Representation.** The Firm will represent you in connection with [DESCRIBE MATTER] (the "Matter"). This engagement does not include [excluded matters, e.g., appeals, tax advice, related litigation] unless we agree in a separate writing.
2. **Client.** The Firm represents [CLIENT NAME] only, and not any affiliated individuals or entities, unless separately agreed.
3. **Fees.** [Hourly: Our fees are based on time at current hourly rates: [ATTORNEY] $[RATE]/hour; [ASSOCIATE] $[RATE]/hour; [PARALEGAL] $[RATE]/hour. Rates may be adjusted periodically.] [OR Flat fee: The fee for the Matter is $[AMOUNT].] [OR Contingency: The Firm's fee will be [%] of any recovery, as detailed in Section 4.]
4. **Costs and Expenses.** You are responsible for out-of-pocket costs (filing fees, court reporters, experts, travel, etc.), which we will advance and bill to you.
5. **Retainer.** You agree to pay an advance retainer of $[AMOUNT], to be held in the Firm's client trust account and applied to fees and costs. You agree to replenish the retainer upon request.
6. **Billing.** We will send invoices [monthly]; payment is due within [30] days. Overdue balances may accrue interest at [RATE] and may result in withdrawal as permitted by the applicable rules of professional conduct.
7. **Client Responsibilities.** You agree to provide accurate information, cooperate, and keep us informed of relevant developments and contact information.
8. **No Guarantee of Outcome.** The Firm will provide diligent representation, but no outcome is guaranteed.
9. **Termination.** You may terminate the engagement at any time in writing. The Firm may withdraw as permitted by the applicable rules of professional conduct. Upon termination, you remain responsible for fees and costs incurred.
10. **File Retention.** After the Matter concludes, the Firm will retain the file for [X] years and may then destroy it.
11. **Dispute Resolution.** [Any fee dispute will be handled through [state bar fee arbitration] / arbitration as described here.]
12. **Governing Rules.** This engagement is governed by the laws of [STATE] and the applicable Rules of Professional Conduct.

Please sign and return the enclosed copy to confirm your agreement. We are pleased to represent you.

Sincerely,
[ATTORNEY NAME], [FIRM NAME]

Agreed and accepted:
_____________________________   Date: __________
[CLIENT NAME]

## Drafting notes
Define the scope precisely and list exclusions — courts and bar authorities look to the engagement letter to determine the scope of duties. Fee terms must be reasonable under Model Rule 1.5; contingency fees must be in writing and signed by the client, and certain matters (domestic relations, criminal defense) cannot be taken on contingency. Confirm no conflicts under Rules 1.7–1.9 before sending and run a conflicts check. Client funds and unearned retainers generally must be held in a trust (IOLTA) account. Some states require specific disclosures (e.g., malpractice insurance status), so verify local rules.

title: Deposition Preparation Checklist
description: Checklist for preparing a witness and counsel for a deposition under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.
body:
# Deposition Preparation Checklist

## Scheduling and logistics
- [ ] Confirm the deposition is properly noticed under FRCP 30 (or subpoena under Rule 45 for non-parties) with correct date, time, and location/remote platform
- [ ] Verify the 7-hour/1-day presumptive time limit (Rule 30(d)(1)) and whether more time is agreed or ordered
- [ ] Arrange the court reporter, videographer (if noticed), and interpreter if needed; confirm remote-deposition technology and exhibit-sharing method
- [ ] Serve any document requests accompanying a Rule 30(b)(2) notice, or the matters for examination for a Rule 30(b)(6) organizational deposition

## Case and document review
- [ ] Review the pleadings, key documents, prior discovery responses, and the witness's prior statements
- [ ] Prepare and organize exhibits with a marking convention; pre-mark where the platform allows
- [ ] Build an outline of topics tied to the elements of claims/defenses and to admissions you want to lock in

## Witness preparation (defending)
- [ ] Meet with the witness to explain the process, the oath, and that the transcript can be used at trial
- [ ] Coach on core rules: tell the truth, listen to the whole question, answer only the question asked, do not guess or speculate, say "I don't know" or "I don't recall" when true, and pause before answering to allow objections
- [ ] Review likely topics and difficult documents without scripting answers; preserve privilege in all prep communications
- [ ] Explain the attorney's limited role: objections are generally to form; instructions not to answer are limited to privilege, a court-ordered limitation, or to present a Rule 30(d)(3) motion

## Taking the deposition (examining)
- [ ] Establish the admonitions/ground rules on the record and confirm the witness understands
- [ ] Lock in background, then proceed chronologically or by topic; use documents to pin down testimony
- [ ] Obtain clear yes/no admissions on key facts; avoid tipping strategy or educating the witness

## Housekeeping
- [ ] Preserve objections to form to avoid waiver under Rule 32(d)(3)
- [ ] Reserve reading and signing of the transcript (Rule 30(e)) as strategy dictates
- [ ] Order the transcript/video and calendar deadlines for errata and any follow-up motions

## Drafting notes
Tailor the depth of witness preparation to the witness's role — a Rule 30(b)(6) corporate designee must be educated on all noticed topics and testifies for the organization, so allocate ample prep time and consider multiple designees. Keep all preparation within the attorney-client privilege and work-product protection, and never instruct a witness to testify falsely. Confirm the governing local rules and the presiding judge's individual practices, which may modify default deposition procedures.

title: Mutual Consent Divorce Petition (HMA Section 13B)
description: Joint petition for divorce by mutual consent under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
body:
# JOINT PETITION FOR DIVORCE BY MUTUAL CONSENT UNDER SECTION 13B OF THE HINDU MARRIAGE ACT, 1955

IN THE COURT OF THE PRINCIPAL JUDGE, FAMILY COURT AT [DISTRICT]

HMA Petition No. ____ of [YEAR]

IN THE MATTER OF:
1. [HUSBAND NAME], son of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], residing at [ADDRESS] — Petitioner No. 1
2. [WIFE NAME], daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], residing at [ADDRESS] — Petitioner No. 2

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Marriage.** The parties were married on [DATE] at [PLACE] according to Hindu rites and ceremonies. A copy of the marriage certificate/photographs is annexed.
2. **Cohabitation and children.** The parties last resided together at [ADDRESS]. [Number] child/children were born of the wedlock, namely [NAMES, AGES]. [State custody arrangement.]
3. **Separation.** The parties have been living separately since [DATE], a period exceeding one year, and have not been able to live together. All efforts at reconciliation have failed.
4. **Free consent.** The parties have mutually and of their own free will, without any force, fraud, coercion, or undue influence, decided to dissolve their marriage.
5. **Settlement of disputes.** All disputes relating to (a) permanent alimony/maintenance, (b) custody and visitation of the child/children, (c) return of streedhan/articles, and (d) any other claims, have been amicably settled as recorded in the accompanying Memorandum of Settlement/terms below:
   a. [Alimony amount and mode of payment.]
   b. [Custody and visitation.]
   c. [Streedhan and articles.]
6. **Jurisdiction.** This Hon'ble Court has jurisdiction as the marriage was solemnised / the parties last resided together / Petitioner No. 2 resides within its territorial limits.
7. **First motion & second motion.** The parties pray for recording of the first motion under Section 13B(1); after the statutory period (which the parties may pray to waive per the settled position in appropriate cases), the parties shall move the second motion under Section 13B(2).
8. **No collusion.** There is no collusion or unnecessary delay; the petition is not presented in collusion within the meaning of the Act.

PRAYER: It is therefore prayed that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to (a) record the first motion; (b) on the second motion, pass a decree of divorce by mutual consent dissolving the marriage between the parties; (c) grant such other relief as deemed fit.

VERIFICATION: Verified at [PLACE] on [DATE] that the contents are true to the knowledge of the petitioners.

[SIGNATURE OF PETITIONER NO. 1]  [SIGNATURE OF PETITIONER NO. 2]
[ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Petitioners

## Drafting notes
- File the first-motion petition jointly with both parties' affidavits; both must appear for recording of statements. Attach the Memorandum of Settlement as an annexure and have both parties sign each page.
- The 6-month cooling-off period under Section 13B(2) is directory and may be waived by the court where the mandated separation is established and settlement is genuine; plead the waiver expressly with supporting facts.
- Ensure maintenance/alimony terms are clear on amount, timing, and finality to avoid future litigation; record that payment is in full and final settlement.
- Address custody, visitation, and education/medical expenses of children explicitly. Keep streedhan return acknowledgements ready to be filed at second motion.

title: Domestic Violence Application (PWDVA Section 12)
description: Application by an aggrieved person under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.
body:
# APPLICATION UNDER SECTION 12 OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ACT, 2005

BEFORE THE COURT OF THE JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS / METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE AT [PLACE]

Application No. ____ of [YEAR]

IN THE MATTER OF:
[AGGRIEVED PERSON NAME], daughter/wife of [NAME], aged [AGE], residing at [ADDRESS] — Applicant/Aggrieved Person

VERSUS

[RESPONDENT NAME(S)], residing at [ADDRESS] — Respondent(s)

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Domestic relationship.** The applicant is in a domestic relationship with the respondent(s) as [wife/live-in partner/family member] and has shared a household at [ADDRESS] within the meaning of Section 2(f) and 2(s).
2. **Acts of domestic violence.** The respondent(s) have subjected the applicant to domestic violence within Section 3, particulars being:
   a. **Physical abuse:** [dates, incidents, injuries, medical records].
   b. **Emotional/verbal abuse:** [insults, threats, humiliation].
   c. **Economic abuse:** [denial of maintenance, dispossession of streedhan, control of finances].
   d. **Sexual abuse:** [as applicable, stated with dignity].
3. **Domestic Incident Report.** A Domestic Incident Report has been / is being recorded by the Protection Officer [NAME], annexed as Annexure [__].
4. **Reliefs sought under the Act:**
   a. **Protection order (Section 18)** restraining the respondent(s) from committing any act of domestic violence, entering the applicant's workplace, or communicating with her.
   b. **Residence order (Section 19)** securing the applicant's right to reside in the shared household / directing alternate accommodation.
   c. **Monetary relief (Section 20)** of Rs. [AMOUNT] towards maintenance, medical expenses, and loss caused.
   d. **Custody order (Section 21)** for temporary custody of the child/children.
   e. **Compensation (Section 22)** of Rs. [AMOUNT] for injuries including mental torture and emotional distress.
5. **Interim/ex parte relief (Section 23).** Pending disposal, the applicant prays for ex parte interim protection and monetary relief.
6. **Jurisdiction.** This Hon'ble Court has jurisdiction as the applicant resides / the respondent resides / the cause of action arose within its limits (Section 27).

PRAYER: It is prayed that this Hon'ble Court grant the reliefs set out above and any further relief deemed just.

VERIFICATION: Verified at [PLACE] on [DATE].

[SIGNATURE OF APPLICANT]
[ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Applicant

## Drafting notes
- File the supporting affidavit in the prescribed Form III; attach the Domestic Incident Report (Form I) if available and medical/police records.
- Seek ex parte interim relief under Section 23 in urgent cases; plead specific, dated incidents to satisfy the prima facie standard.
- Remember reliefs under the DV Act are civil in nature and can be sought in addition to remedies under BNS/matrimonial law; coordinate with any parallel maintenance (BNSS 144) or divorce proceedings.
- Keep the narrative dignified and chronological; courts respond to specificity of dates, places, and corroboration.

title: Last Will and Testament (India)
description: A simple last will and testament for an individual under the Indian Succession Act, 1925.
body:
# LAST WILL AND TESTAMENT

I, [TESTATOR NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], resident of [ADDRESS], [PAN/AADHAAR ref], being of sound mind, memory, and understanding, and not acting under any coercion, fraud, or undue influence, do hereby make, publish, and declare this to be my Last Will and Testament, revoking all prior wills and codicils made by me.

1. **Declaration.** I declare that I am a [Hindu/Christian/Parsi] and this Will is executed voluntarily in a sound disposing state of mind.
2. **Family.** I am married to [SPOUSE NAME]. My children are [NAMES, AGES]. [State any dependents.]
3. **Executor.** I appoint [EXECUTOR NAME], resident of [ADDRESS], as the Executor of this Will. If they are unable or unwilling to act, I appoint [ALTERNATE EXECUTOR] as substitute Executor. The Executor shall not be required to furnish any security.
4. **Immovable property.** I bequeath my immovable property being [DESCRIPTION AND ADDRESS, survey/plot numbers] to [BENEFICIARY NAME] absolutely.
5. **Movable property and financial assets.** I bequeath my bank accounts ([BANK, ACCOUNT NOS.]), fixed deposits, shares, mutual funds ([FOLIO/DEMAT DETAILS]), jewellery, and other movables to [BENEFICIARY NAME(S)] in the following manner: [SPECIFY SHARES/PROPORTIONS].
6. **Residuary clause.** All the rest, residue, and remainder of my estate, whether movable or immovable, wheresoever situated, and not specifically disposed of above, I give to [RESIDUARY BENEFICIARY].
7. **Specific bequests.** [Any charitable donations, gifts to friends, etc.]
8. **Guardianship.** In the event of my death while any child is a minor, I appoint [GUARDIAN NAME] as guardian of the person and property of such minor.
9. **No contest.** Any beneficiary who contests this Will shall forfeit their bequest, which shall fall into the residue. [Adjust as instructed.]
10. **Execution.** I have signed this Will consisting of [NUMBER] pages on [DATE] at [PLACE].

SIGNED by the above-named Testator [TESTATOR NAME] as their Last Will and Testament in our presence, both being present at the same time, and we have, in the presence of the Testator and of each other, subscribed our names as witnesses:

WITNESS 1: [NAME, ADDRESS, SIGNATURE]
WITNESS 2: [NAME, ADDRESS, SIGNATURE]

## Drafting notes
- A Will must be signed by the testator and attested by at least two witnesses who saw the testator sign (Section 63, Indian Succession Act, 1925). Witnesses should not be beneficiaries.
- Registration is optional but advisable to reduce challenges; note that Muslims are governed by personal law and this template does not apply to them.
- Consider a self-declaration of sound mind, a doctor's certificate for elderly testators, and dated pagination on every page with initials to prevent tampering.
- Keep an inventory of assets updated; a residuary clause avoids intestacy over omitted assets. Revisit the Will after major life events (marriage, birth, property acquisition).

title: Gift Deed (India)
description: Deed of gift of immovable property by a donor to a donee under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.
body:
# GIFT DEED

This Deed of Gift is executed at [PLACE] on this [DATE] BETWEEN:

[DONOR NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], resident of [ADDRESS] (hereinafter the "Donor", which expression shall include heirs, executors, and administrators);

AND

[DONEE NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], aged [AGE], resident of [ADDRESS] (hereinafter the "Donee", which expression shall include heirs, executors, and administrators).

WHEREAS the Donor is the absolute owner, in lawful and peaceful possession, of the immovable property more particularly described in the Schedule below (the "Property"), having acquired it by [mode of acquisition, e.g., sale deed dated __ / inheritance];

AND WHEREAS the Donor, out of natural love and affection for the Donee (who is the Donor's [relationship]), and without any monetary consideration, desires to gift the Property to the Donee;

NOW THIS DEED WITNESSETH as follows:

1. **Gift.** In consideration of natural love and affection and without any monetary consideration, the Donor hereby voluntarily gifts, transfers, and conveys the Property to the Donee absolutely and forever, together with all rights, easements, and appurtenances.
2. **Acceptance.** The Donee hereby accepts the gift of the Property.
3. **Delivery of possession.** The Donor has delivered vacant and peaceful possession of the Property to the Donee, who is now the absolute owner.
4. **Free from encumbrances.** The Donor covenants that the Property is free from all encumbrances, charges, liens, attachments, and litigation, and that the Donor has full right and authority to gift the same.
5. **Irrevocability.** This gift is absolute and irrevocable. The Donor shall have no right, title, or interest in the Property henceforth.
6. **Mutation and taxes.** The Donee shall be entitled to have the Property mutated in their name in the revenue/municipal records and shall pay all future taxes.
7. **Indemnity.** The Donor shall indemnify the Donee against any loss arising from any defect in the Donor's title.

SCHEDULE OF PROPERTY: [Full description — survey/plot no., area, boundaries (north/south/east/west), address.]

IN WITNESS WHEREOF the parties have signed this Deed on the date first written above.

DONOR: [SIGNATURE]      DONEE: [SIGNATURE]
WITNESS 1: [NAME, SIGNATURE]   WITNESS 2: [NAME, SIGNATURE]

## Drafting notes
- A gift of immovable property must be effected by a registered instrument attested by at least two witnesses (Section 123, Transfer of Property Act, 1882) and registered under the Registration Act, 1908.
- Acceptance by the donee during the donor's lifetime and while capable is essential; record delivery of possession expressly.
- Stamp duty on gift deeds varies by State and by relationship (concessional rates often apply for close relatives); verify current State schedule before execution.
- A validly completed gift is irrevocable except on grounds under Section 126 TPA; if conditions are intended, draft them carefully as they may render the gift onerous or conditional.

title: Agreement to Sell Immovable Property (India)
description: Agreement to sell immovable property between a seller and buyer under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.
body:
# AGREEMENT TO SELL

This Agreement to Sell is made at [PLACE] on [DATE] BETWEEN:

[SELLER NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], resident of [ADDRESS] (the "Seller");

AND

[BUYER NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], resident of [ADDRESS] (the "Buyer").

WHEREAS the Seller is the absolute owner in possession of the property described in the Schedule (the "Property"), free from encumbrances, and has agreed to sell it to the Buyer, who has agreed to purchase it, on the terms below.

NOW IT IS AGREED as follows:

1. **Sale consideration.** The total sale consideration is Rs. [AMOUNT] (Rupees [WORDS]).
2. **Payment schedule.**
   a. Rs. [AMOUNT] paid as earnest money/advance on execution (receipt acknowledged).
   b. Balance of Rs. [AMOUNT] payable at the time of registration of the sale deed on or before [DATE].
3. **Title and documents.** The Seller shall make out a clear and marketable title and hand over all original title documents, tax receipts, encumbrance certificate, and approved plans on or before completion.
4. **Vacant possession.** The Seller shall deliver vacant, peaceful, and physical possession of the Property to the Buyer at the time of registration of the sale deed.
5. **Encumbrances and dues.** The Seller warrants the Property is free from all encumbrances, charges, litigation, and statutory dues up to the date of registration; all arrears of tax, electricity, and maintenance up to that date are the Seller's liability.
6. **Completion.** The sale shall be completed by execution and registration of the sale deed within [TIME] of the Buyer's satisfactory title verification.
7. **Default and remedies.**
   a. If the Buyer defaults, the earnest money may be forfeited.
   b. If the Seller defaults, the Buyer may seek refund with interest and/or specific performance under the Specific Relief Act, 1963.
8. **Stamp duty and registration.** Stamp duty and registration charges on the sale deed shall be borne by the [Buyer/as agreed].
9. **Time of essence.** Time is of the essence for payment and completion, subject to reasonable extension by mutual consent.
10. **Dispute resolution and jurisdiction.** Disputes shall be [arbitrated under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 / subject to the courts at [CITY]].

SCHEDULE OF PROPERTY: [Survey/plot no., area, boundaries, address, and share, if any.]

IN WITNESS WHEREOF the parties have signed this Agreement on the date first written above.

SELLER: [SIGNATURE]   BUYER: [SIGNATURE]
WITNESS 1: [NAME]   WITNESS 2: [NAME]

## Drafting notes
- An agreement to sell does not itself transfer ownership (Section 54, TPA); title passes only on a registered sale deed. Keep the conveyance deed as a separate, subsequent instrument.
- Conduct title due diligence: 30-year title chain, encumbrance certificate, mutation records, approved building plans, and no-dues certificates before paying the balance.
- State stamp duty on agreements to sell varies; where possession is delivered under the agreement, some States treat it as a conveyance for stamp purposes — verify locally.
- Draft default and forfeiture clauses carefully; preserve the buyer's specific-performance remedy and provide for refund with interest on the seller's default.

title: Suit for Specific Performance (Specific Relief Act, 1963)
description: Plaint for specific performance of an agreement to sell immovable property under the Specific Relief Act, 1963.
body:
# PLAINT FOR SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE UNDER THE SPECIFIC RELIEF ACT, 1963

IN THE COURT OF THE [CIVIL JUDGE / DISTRICT JUDGE] AT [DISTRICT]

Suit No. ____ of [YEAR]

[PLAINTIFF NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], resident of [ADDRESS] — Plaintiff

VERSUS

[DEFENDANT NAME], son/daughter of [FATHER'S NAME], resident of [ADDRESS] — Defendant

The Plaintiff above-named most respectfully submits:

1. **The agreement.** By an Agreement to Sell dated [DATE], the Defendant agreed to sell to the Plaintiff the immovable property described in the Schedule (the "Property") for a total consideration of Rs. [AMOUNT], of which the Plaintiff paid Rs. [AMOUNT] as earnest money (receipt acknowledged).
2. **Terms.** Under the agreement, the sale deed was to be executed and registered on or before [DATE] upon payment of the balance consideration of Rs. [AMOUNT].
3. **Readiness and willingness.** The Plaintiff has always been, and continues to be, ready and willing to perform their part of the contract, including payment of the balance consideration, as required by Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963. [State proof — funds available, notices calling for execution, etc.]
4. **Breach by Defendant.** Despite the Plaintiff's readiness and repeated requests/notices dated [DATES], the Defendant has failed and neglected to execute the sale deed and is attempting to [resile / sell to a third party].
5. **Legal notice.** The Plaintiff issued a legal notice dated [DATE] calling upon the Defendant to perform, which has gone unheeded / been wrongly replied.
6. **Cause of action** arose on [DATE] when the Defendant failed to execute the sale deed, and is continuing; the suit is within limitation (three years from the date fixed for performance, Article 54, Limitation Act, 1963).
7. **Jurisdiction and valuation.** The Property is situated within this Court's territorial jurisdiction; the suit is valued at Rs. [AMOUNT] for court fees and jurisdiction.

PRAYER: The Plaintiff prays that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to:
(a) direct the Defendant to specifically perform the Agreement dated [DATE] by executing and registering the sale deed on receipt of the balance consideration;
(b) in the alternative, decree refund of Rs. [AMOUNT] with interest and damages;
(c) grant a permanent injunction restraining the Defendant from alienating or encumbering the Property;
(d) award costs and such other relief as deemed fit.

SCHEDULE OF PROPERTY: [Description with boundaries.]

VERIFICATION: Verified at [PLACE] on [DATE].

[PLAINTIFF SIGNATURE]
[ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Plaintiff

## Drafting notes
- Post-2018 amendment, specific performance is a general rule rather than a discretionary remedy (Sections 10 and 20, SRA 1963); plead entitlement accordingly and avoid framing it as merely equitable.
- Continuous readiness and willingness (Section 16(c)) is essential — plead and prove it with particulars (funds, tender, notices). Deposit the balance in court if directed.
- Seek an interim injunction (Order XXXIX Rules 1-2 CPC) against third-party alienation to protect the subject matter; consider lis pendens under Section 52 TPA.
- Watch limitation: three years from the date fixed for performance, or from when the plaintiff had notice of refusal (Article 54). Plead the alternative relief of refund with interest to preserve fallback.

title: Consumer Appeal to State Commission (CPA 2019)
description: Appeal to the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission against a District Commission order under Section 41 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
body:
# APPEAL UNDER SECTION 41 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019

BEFORE THE STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION AT [STATE]

Appeal No. ____ of [YEAR]
(Arising out of order dated [DATE] in Consumer Complaint No. ____ of [YEAR] passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission at [DISTRICT])

[APPELLANT NAME], [ADDRESS] — Appellant (Original Complainant/Opposite Party)

VERSUS

[RESPONDENT NAME], [ADDRESS] — Respondent

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Impugned order.** The Appellant is aggrieved by the order dated [DATE] passed by the District Commission at [DISTRICT] in Complaint No. ____, whereby [summarise the operative order].
2. **Parties and background.** [Brief statement of the parties and the underlying transaction/service and the deficiency/defect alleged.]
3. **Limitation.** The impugned order was received on [DATE]; this appeal is filed within the 45-day period prescribed under Section 41. [If delayed, an application for condonation of delay with sufficient cause is filed separately.]
4. **Pre-deposit.** Where the Appellant is the person directed to pay any amount, 50% of the amount ordered has been deposited as required by the proviso to Section 41. [Attach proof.]
5. **Grounds of appeal:**
   A. The District Commission erred in appreciating the evidence on record and reached a finding contrary to the material.
   B. The District Commission wrongly held [finding] despite [reason]; the finding is perverse and unsustainable.
   C. The relief granted/denied is [excessive/inadequate/contrary to law].
   D. The District Commission failed to consider [document/contention].
   E. [Any jurisdictional or procedural error.]
6. **Interim relief.** The Appellant prays for a stay of the operation of the impugned order pending disposal of this appeal.

PRAYER: It is prayed that this Hon'ble Commission be pleased to (a) set aside/modify the order dated [DATE]; (b) grant [relief]; (c) stay the impugned order pending disposal; (d) grant costs and such other relief as deemed fit.

VERIFICATION: Verified at [PLACE] on [DATE].

[APPELLANT SIGNATURE]
[ADVOCATE NAME], Counsel for the Appellant

Annexures: [Certified copy of impugned order, memo of parties, proof of pre-deposit, relevant documents.]

## Drafting notes
- The appeal must be filed within 45 days of the District Commission's order (Section 41); attach a condonation application with a supporting affidavit if late, showing sufficient cause.
- If the appellant is directed to pay a sum, 50% pre-deposit is a mandatory pre-condition to entertaining the appeal (proviso to Section 41) — file proof of deposit up front.
- Attach a certified copy of the impugned order and a concise memo of grounds; focus grounds on errors of law and perversity of findings, not mere re-argument of facts.
- Seek stay of the impugned order early; remember further appeal to the NCDRC (Section 51) is available only in limited circumstances.

title: RTI Application (Right to Information Act, 2005)
description: Application to a Public Information Officer seeking information under Section 6 of the Right to Information Act, 2005.
body:
# APPLICATION UNDER SECTION 6 OF THE RIGHT TO INFORMATION ACT, 2005

To,
The Public Information Officer (PIO),
[NAME OF PUBLIC AUTHORITY / DEPARTMENT]
[ADDRESS]

From,
[APPLICANT NAME]
[FULL POSTAL ADDRESS]
[EMAIL / PHONE]

Date: [DATE]

Subject: Request for information under the Right to Information Act, 2005.

Sir/Madam,

Under Section 6 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, I request the following information from your public authority:

1. [Specific query 1 — clearly worded, with relevant dates/reference numbers.]
2. [Specific query 2 — e.g., certified copies of documents, file notings, order sheets.]
3. [Specific query 3 — e.g., status of application/complaint no. ____ dated ____.]
4. [Specific query 4 — names/designations of officials who dealt with the matter.]
5. [Specific query 5 — inspection of records on a mutually convenient date, if applicable.]

**Period of information sought:** [From DATE to DATE].
**Form of information:** [Certified photocopies / soft copy / inspection of records].

DECLARATIONS:
- I am a citizen of India.
- I have paid the prescribed application fee of Rs. 10 by [IPO / DD / court fee stamp / online], details: [REF].
- If I belong to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category, a copy of the BPL certificate is enclosed and no fee is payable.
- If the information sought is voluminous, kindly inform me of the additional cost as per the RTI Rules before processing.

Kindly furnish the above information within the 30-day period prescribed under Section 7 of the Act. If any part of the information is held by another public authority, kindly transfer that portion under Section 6(3) and inform me. If the request is rejected in whole or part, kindly provide reasons and details of the First Appellate Authority under Section 19.

Thanking you,
Yours faithfully,
[APPLICANT SIGNATURE]
[APPLICANT NAME]

## Drafting notes
- Frame queries as specific requests for information/records, not as questions seeking opinions or hypothetical answers, which are outside the Act's scope.
- The standard fee is Rs. 10 (waived for BPL applicants); additional copying/inspection charges apply per the RTI Rules and must be paid before dispatch.
- The PIO must respond within 30 days (48 hours where life or liberty is involved). Note the exemptions under Section 8 and the third-party procedure under Section 11.
- If there is no or an unsatisfactory response, a First Appeal lies to the First Appellate Authority within 30 days (Section 19(1)), and thereafter a Second Appeal to the Information Commission within 90 days (Section 19(3)).

title: Last Will and Testament (US)
description: A simple last will and testament for an individual, with state-specific execution formalities as placeholders.
body:
# LAST WILL AND TESTAMENT OF [TESTATOR NAME]

I, [TESTATOR NAME], a resident of [CITY], [COUNTY] County, [STATE], being of sound mind and memory and not acting under duress, fraud, or undue influence, declare this to be my Last Will and Testament, and I revoke all prior wills and codicils.

**ARTICLE I — Family.** I am [married to / unmarried]. [If married: My spouse's name is [SPOUSE NAME].] My children are: [NAMES]. References to "my children" include children later born or adopted.

**ARTICLE II — Payment of Debts and Expenses.** I direct my Executor to pay my legally enforceable debts, funeral expenses, and expenses of administering my estate as soon as practicable.

**ARTICLE III — Specific Bequests.** I give the following specific gifts:
(a) [DESCRIBE ITEM] to [BENEFICIARY].
(b) The sum of $[AMOUNT] to [BENEFICIARY].
If a beneficiary does not survive me by [30] days, the gift lapses and becomes part of my residuary estate.

**ARTICLE IV — Residuary Estate.** I give all the rest, residue, and remainder of my estate, of every kind and wherever located, to [RESIDUARY BENEFICIARY]; if they do not survive me, then to [ALTERNATE BENEFICIARY], per stirpes.

**ARTICLE V — Appointment of Executor.** I nominate [EXECUTOR NAME] as Executor. If they are unable or unwilling to serve, I nominate [ALTERNATE EXECUTOR]. I direct that my Executor serve without bond and have all powers permitted under [STATE] law, including the power to sell, lease, and distribute estate property without court order where allowed.

**ARTICLE VI — Guardian for Minor Children.** If any child of mine is a minor at my death, I nominate [GUARDIAN NAME] as guardian of the person and estate of such minor child; if unable to serve, [ALTERNATE GUARDIAN].

**ARTICLE VII — No-Contest.** If any beneficiary contests this Will, any gift to that person is revoked, to the extent permitted by [STATE] law.

**ARTICLE VIII — Governing Law.** This Will is governed by the laws of the State of [STATE].

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I sign this Will on [DATE].

_______________________  [TESTATOR NAME], Testator

**ATTESTATION.** The foregoing instrument was signed by the Testator in our presence, and we, at the Testator's request and in the presence of the Testator and of each other, subscribe our names as witnesses, believing the Testator to be of sound mind and under no constraint.

WITNESS 1: [NAME, ADDRESS, SIGNATURE]
WITNESS 2: [NAME, ADDRESS, SIGNATURE]

[SELF-PROVING AFFIDAVIT / NOTARY BLOCK — attach per [STATE] law.]

## Drafting notes
- Execution formalities are governed by state law; most states require the testator's signature and two disinterested witnesses. Confirm [STATE] requirements before signing.
- A self-proving affidavit (signed before a notary) streamlines probate in many states — include the state-specific form.
- Avoid interested witnesses; a witness who is also a beneficiary may forfeit or reduce their gift in some states.
- Coordinate with beneficiary designations on non-probate assets (life insurance, retirement accounts, POD/TOD accounts), which pass outside the Will. Consider a revocable living trust for larger or multi-state estates.

title: Durable Power of Attorney (US)
description: A durable financial power of attorney appointing an agent to act on the principal's behalf, with state-specific formalities as placeholders.
body:
# DURABLE POWER OF ATTORNEY

**Principal:** [PRINCIPAL NAME], residing at [ADDRESS], [CITY], [STATE].
**Agent (Attorney-in-Fact):** [AGENT NAME], residing at [ADDRESS].
**Successor Agent:** [SUCCESSOR AGENT NAME], residing at [ADDRESS].

1. **Appointment.** I, [PRINCIPAL NAME], appoint the Agent named above as my attorney-in-fact to act for me in my name and on my behalf as set out below. If the Agent is unable or unwilling to serve, the Successor Agent shall serve.
2. **Durability.** This Power of Attorney is DURABLE. It shall not be affected by my subsequent disability or incapacity and shall remain in effect until my death or until revoked by me in writing. (Governed by [STATE]'s adoption of the Uniform Power of Attorney Act or equivalent statute.)
3. **Effective date.** This Power of Attorney is effective [immediately upon execution / upon my incapacity as certified by a licensed physician].
4. **Powers granted.** I grant my Agent authority with respect to the following (initial or strike as applicable):
   (a) Real property transactions;
   (b) Tangible personal property transactions;
   (c) Banking and other financial-institution transactions;
   (d) Stocks, bonds, and other investment transactions;
   (e) Business operating transactions;
   (f) Insurance and annuity transactions;
   (g) Estate, trust, and beneficiary transactions;
   (h) Claims and litigation;
   (i) Tax matters, including filing returns and dealing with the IRS and [STATE] tax authorities;
   (j) Government benefits and retirement-plan transactions.
5. **Standard of care.** The Agent shall act in good faith, in my best interest, with care, competence, and diligence, keep records, and avoid conflicts of interest and self-dealing except as expressly authorized.
6. **Compensation and reimbursement.** The Agent [shall / shall not] be entitled to reasonable compensation and shall be reimbursed for reasonable expenses.
7. **Third-party reliance.** Any third party may rely on this Power of Attorney and on the Agent's authority; I agree to indemnify any third party who acts in good-faith reliance.
8. **Revocation.** I may revoke this instrument at any time by a signed writing delivered to the Agent.
9. **Governing law.** This instrument is governed by the laws of the State of [STATE].

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I sign this Durable Power of Attorney on [DATE].

_______________________  [PRINCIPAL NAME], Principal

WITNESS 1: [NAME, SIGNATURE]   WITNESS 2: [NAME, SIGNATURE]

STATE OF [STATE], COUNTY OF [COUNTY] — Acknowledged before me on [DATE] by [PRINCIPAL NAME].
[NOTARY PUBLIC SIGNATURE AND SEAL]

**Agent's Acknowledgment (if required by [STATE]):** I, [AGENT NAME], accept appointment and agree to act in the Principal's best interest.

## Drafting notes
- Execution formalities vary by state; many require notarization and/or two witnesses. Confirm [STATE] requirements and any statutory short-form language.
- "Durable" language ensures the power survives incapacity; a "springing" power takes effect only on incapacity but can complicate proof — specify the incapacity-determination mechanism.
- Certain "hot powers" (making gifts, changing beneficiary designations, creating/amending trusts, delegating authority) often must be expressly and separately granted under the Uniform Power of Attorney Act.
- Provide financial institutions with certified copies; some banks require their own forms. Record the POA with the county recorder if it authorizes real-property transactions.

title: Residential Lease Agreement (US)
description: A residential lease agreement between a landlord and tenant, with state-specific terms as placeholders.
body:
# RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT

This Residential Lease Agreement (the "Lease") is made on [DATE] between [LANDLORD NAME] ("Landlord") and [TENANT NAME(S)] ("Tenant").

1. **Premises.** Landlord leases to Tenant the residential premises located at [ADDRESS], [CITY], [STATE], [ZIP] (the "Premises").
2. **Term.** The Lease begins on [START DATE] and ends on [END DATE] (a fixed term of [MONTHS] months). [Or: month-to-month tenancy beginning [DATE].]
3. **Rent.** Tenant shall pay rent of $[AMOUNT] per month, due on the [1st] day of each month, payable to Landlord at [ADDRESS/METHOD]. A late fee of $[AMOUNT] applies if rent is more than [NUMBER] days late, to the extent permitted by [STATE] law.
4. **Security deposit.** Tenant shall pay a security deposit of $[AMOUNT], to be held and returned in accordance with [STATE] law, less lawful deductions, within [STATE-REQUIRED DAYS] after the Tenant vacates.
5. **Occupancy.** The Premises shall be occupied only by the Tenant(s) named and [NAMES of authorized occupants] as a private residence.
6. **Utilities.** Tenant is responsible for [LIST UTILITIES]; Landlord is responsible for [LIST UTILITIES].
7. **Maintenance and repairs.** Tenant shall keep the Premises clean and undamaged and promptly report needed repairs. Landlord shall maintain the Premises in habitable condition as required by [STATE] law (implied warranty of habitability).
8. **Use and conduct.** Tenant shall not use the Premises for unlawful purposes, shall not disturb neighbors, and shall comply with all applicable laws and any attached rules.
9. **Pets.** [No pets / Pets allowed subject to a pet deposit of $[AMOUNT] and the following conditions.]
10. **Alterations.** Tenant shall not make alterations without Landlord's prior written consent.
11. **Entry.** Landlord may enter the Premises for inspection, repairs, or showings upon [STATE-REQUIRED] notice (typically 24 hours), except in emergencies.
12. **Assignment/Subletting.** Tenant shall not assign or sublet without Landlord's prior written consent.
13. **Default.** If Tenant fails to pay rent or breaches the Lease, Landlord may pursue remedies under [STATE] law, including service of the required notice and eviction proceedings.
14. **Disclosures.** Landlord provides all disclosures required by law, including the federal lead-based paint disclosure for pre-1978 housing and any [STATE]-required disclosures.
15. **Governing law.** This Lease is governed by the laws of the State of [STATE].

LANDLORD: _______________  TENANT: _______________  DATE: [DATE]

## Drafting notes
- Landlord-tenant law is heavily state- and often city-specific; verify [STATE] rules on security-deposit limits and return deadlines, late fees, notice periods, and habitability before use.
- The federal lead-based paint disclosure (and EPA pamphlet) is mandatory for housing built before 1978; failure to provide it carries penalties.
- Rent-control or rent-stabilization ordinances (e.g., in some California and New York jurisdictions) may override lease terms; check local law.
- Keep entry-notice, repair, and habitability clauses compliant; unenforceable clauses (e.g., waivers of habitability) can void portions of the lease. Document the move-in condition with a signed checklist and photos.

title: Eviction Notice / Notice to Quit (US)
description: Notice to a tenant to pay rent or quit / to vacate the premises, with state-specific timeframes as placeholders.
body:
# NOTICE TO [PAY RENT OR QUIT / CURE OR QUIT / VACATE]

Date: [DATE]

To: [TENANT NAME(S)] and all others in possession
Premises: [ADDRESS], [CITY], [STATE], [ZIP] (the "Premises")

1. **Notice.** YOU ARE HEREBY NOTIFIED that you are in violation of your tenancy of the above Premises for the reason(s) checked below:
   [ ] **Non-payment of rent.** Rent in the amount of $[AMOUNT], covering the period from [DATE] to [DATE], is past due and unpaid.
   [ ] **Lease violation (curable).** You have violated the following term(s) of your lease: [DESCRIBE VIOLATION].
   [ ] **Termination of month-to-month tenancy.** Your month-to-month tenancy is terminated.
   [ ] **Other:** [DESCRIBE].
2. **Action required.** Within [STATE-REQUIRED NUMBER] days after service of this Notice, you must:
   [ ] Pay the full amount of rent due ($[AMOUNT]) to [LANDLORD/AGENT NAME] at [ADDRESS/METHOD]; OR
   [ ] Cure the lease violation described above; OR
   [ ] Vacate and surrender possession of the Premises.
3. **Consequence of non-compliance.** If you fail to pay/cure or vacate within the time stated, the Landlord will terminate your tenancy and commence eviction (unlawful detainer/summary process) proceedings against you in accordance with [STATE] law, seeking possession of the Premises, unpaid rent, damages, and court costs, and, where permitted, attorney's fees.
4. **No waiver.** Acceptance of any partial payment does not waive the Landlord's rights or this Notice unless agreed in writing.
5. **Reservation of rights.** This Notice is given without waiving, and with full reservation of, all of the Landlord's rights and remedies under the lease and applicable law.

[LANDLORD / AGENT NAME]
[ADDRESS]  [PHONE]
Signature: _______________

**PROOF OF SERVICE:** I served this Notice on [DATE] by [personal delivery / substituted service / posting and mailing] in the manner required by [STATE] law.
Server: [NAME, SIGNATURE]

## Drafting notes
- Notice periods and permissible grounds are strictly governed by state (and often local) law; a defective notice period or method is the most common reason evictions are dismissed. Verify [STATE] requirements.
- Use the correct notice type: pay-or-quit for nonpayment, cure-or-quit for curable violations, unconditional quit where allowed, and a proper termination notice for month-to-month tenancies.
- Serve strictly in the manner the statute requires (personal, substituted, or post-and-mail) and keep a dated proof of service; self-help eviction (lockouts, utility shutoffs) is illegal in every state.
- After the notice period expires without compliance, the landlord must file a court eviction (unlawful detainer/summary process) — the notice alone does not authorize removal of the tenant.

title: Prenuptial Agreement (US)
description: A premarital (prenuptial) agreement between two prospective spouses, with state-specific formalities as placeholders.
body:
# PRENUPTIAL AGREEMENT

This Prenuptial Agreement (the "Agreement") is made on [DATE] between [PARTY A NAME] ("Party A") and [PARTY B NAME] ("Party B"), who intend to marry on or about [DATE].

**RECITALS.**
A. The parties intend to marry and wish to define their respective property rights and obligations during marriage and in the event of separation, divorce, or death.
B. Each party has made a full and fair disclosure of assets, liabilities, and income, as set out in the attached Schedules A (Party A) and B (Party B).
C. Each party has had the opportunity to consult independent legal counsel and enters this Agreement voluntarily, without duress or undue influence.

NOW, THEREFORE, the parties agree:

1. **Separate property.** All property owned by each party before the marriage, and all property later acquired by gift, inheritance, or with separate-property funds, shall remain that party's separate property, together with any appreciation, income, and proceeds thereof.
2. **Marital/community property.** [Define what will be treated as marital/community property and how it will be divided on divorce, consistent with [STATE] law.]
3. **Income and earnings.** [State whether earnings during marriage are separate or marital.]
4. **Debts.** Each party shall be solely responsible for debts incurred in that party's own name before and during the marriage, except [jointly incurred debts as agreed].
5. **Spousal support / alimony.** [Waiver, limitation, or agreed formula for spousal support, to the extent enforceable under [STATE] law.]
6. **Property on death.** Nothing in this Agreement limits a party's right to make voluntary gifts or bequests to the other. [Address elective-share/statutory rights as permitted.]
7. **Marital residence.** [Ownership, occupancy, and disposition of the marital home.]
8. **Full disclosure.** Each party acknowledges receipt of the other's financial disclosures (Schedules A and B) and that the disclosures are fair and reasonable.
9. **Independent counsel.** Each party acknowledges the opportunity to be represented by independent counsel of their choosing; [Party ___ was / was not represented, having knowingly waived counsel].
10. **Voluntariness.** Each party signs freely and voluntarily, without coercion, and with adequate time for review before the wedding.
11. **Severability.** If any provision is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in effect.
12. **Governing law.** This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of [STATE], consistent with the Uniform Premarital Agreement Act as adopted, where applicable.
13. **Amendment.** This Agreement may be amended only by a writing signed by both parties.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties sign this Agreement on the date above.

PARTY A: _______________   PARTY B: _______________

STATE OF [STATE], COUNTY OF [COUNTY] — Acknowledged before me on [DATE].
[NOTARY PUBLIC SIGNATURE AND SEAL]

Schedule A — Party A's Assets, Liabilities, and Income
Schedule B — Party B's Assets, Liabilities, and Income

## Drafting notes
- Enforceability turns on voluntary execution, full and fair financial disclosure, and (in many states) the opportunity for independent counsel; sign well before the wedding to rebut claims of duress.
- Many states follow the Uniform Premarital Agreement Act (or UPMAA); some impose extra requirements. Confirm [STATE] rules, especially on spousal-support waivers, which some states scrutinize or limit.
- Provisions purporting to govern child custody or child support are generally unenforceable — those are decided by the court under the best-interests standard.
- Attach complete financial schedules and have the Agreement notarized; consider separate legal counsel memos and a waiting period between presentation and signing to strengthen enforceability.

title: POSH Internal Committee Inquiry Checklist (India)
description: Checklist for conducting an inquiry into a workplace sexual harassment complaint by the Internal Committee under the POSH Act, 2013.
body:
# POSH Internal Committee Inquiry Checklist

- [ ] Verify the Internal Committee (IC) is validly constituted under Section 4: Presiding Officer (senior woman employee), at least two employee members committed to women's causes or with relevant experience, and one external member from an NGO/association familiar with sexual harassment issues; at least half the members are women
- [ ] Confirm the complaint is in writing (six copies as far as practicable) and filed within three months of the incident (extendable up to a further three months for sufficient reasons) per Section 9
- [ ] Check the complaint falls within "sexual harassment" (Section 2(n)) and "workplace" (Section 2(o)); confirm the aggrieved woman and respondent's status
- [ ] Offer conciliation at the aggrieved woman's request before inquiry (Section 10); if settled, record terms — but no monetary settlement as a basis of conciliation
- [ ] Provide the respondent a copy of the complaint within the prescribed time and seek a written reply with supporting documents and witness list
- [ ] Ensure principles of natural justice: fair hearing, opportunity to lead evidence, cross-examination through the IC (not direct confrontation), and no ex parte action without notice
- [ ] Maintain confidentiality (Section 16): identities of the aggrieved woman, respondent, witnesses, and contents must not be published or disclosed
- [ ] Consider interim relief during pendency (Section 12): transfer, leave (up to three months), or restraining reporting relationships
- [ ] Conduct the inquiry with the powers of a civil court (summoning, evidence) and document each sitting with signed minutes and attendance
- [ ] Complete the inquiry within 90 days (Section 11(4)); prepare the inquiry report within 10 days of completion and share it with both parties (Section 13)
- [ ] Record findings on whether the allegation is proved on the balance of probabilities; recommend action under service rules or the Rules (Section 13) — no penalty for false/malicious complaints without proof of malice (Section 14)
- [ ] Ensure the employer acts on recommendations within 60 days; advise the aggrieved woman of appeal rights (Section 18) within 90 days
- [ ] Update the annual report (Section 21) and confirm the organisation's POSH policy, awareness programs, and register of complaints are current

**Practical notes:**
- Confirm the ICC is properly constituted (Presiding Officer, requisite members, and the external member).
- Observe the principles of natural justice and strict confidentiality throughout the inquiry.
- Adhere to statutory timelines: 90 days for inquiry, 10 days for the report, and 60 days for action.
- Advise the aggrieved woman of appeal rights (Section 18) within 90 days.
- Maintain the register of complaints and file the annual report (Section 21).

title: Mutual NDA (US Federal / Multi-State)
description: Mutual non-disclosure agreement suitable for US commercial diligence.
body:
# MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of [DATE] by and between [PARTY A] and [PARTY B] (each a "Party").

## 1. Purpose
The Parties wish to explore [TRANSACTION] and may disclose Confidential Information.

## 2. Definition of Confidential Information
"Confidential Information" means non-public information disclosed by a Party, including business, technical, financial, and customer information, whether marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential.

## 3. Obligations
Each Party shall (a) use Confidential Information only for the Purpose; (b) protect it with at least reasonable care; and (c) not disclose it to third parties except to advisors under confidentiality obligations.

## 4. Exclusions
Obligations do not apply to information that is public, independently developed, rightfully received, or required to be disclosed by law (with notice where legally permitted).

## 5. Term
Obligations survive for [3/5] years after disclosure; trade secrets remain protected while they qualify as trade secrets.

## 6. Return / Destruction
Upon request, the receiving Party shall return or destroy Confidential Information, except one archival copy retained for legal/compliance purposes.

## 7. Governing Law
Governing law: [State], USA. Venue: [County/State] courts.

**Drafting notes:** Confirm residual clauses, residuals carve-outs, and export-control language for tech deals.

title: Employment Offer Letter (At-Will, US)
description: At-will employment offer letter skeleton for US employers.
body:
# EMPLOYMENT OFFER LETTER

[DATE]

[CANDIDATE NAME]
[ADDRESS]

Dear [CANDIDATE]:

We are pleased to offer you the position of [TITLE] with [COMPANY], reporting to [MANAGER], starting on [START DATE], based in [LOCATION] / remote.

**Compensation.** Base salary $[AMOUNT] per [year/month], paid [biweekly], less applicable withholdings. You may be eligible for [bonus/equity] subject to plan terms.

**Benefits.** Eligible for company benefits after [waiting period], including [medical/dental/401k], subject to plan documents.

**At-will employment.** Employment is at-will and may be terminated by either party at any time, with or without cause or notice, subject to applicable law.

**Contingencies.** This offer is contingent on [background check / work authorization / signed confidentiality / arbitration agreement].

**Governing policies.** You agree to comply with company policies as updated from time to time.

Please sign and return by [DEADLINE].

Sincerely,
[SIGNATORY]

Accepted: ________________  Date: ________

**Drafting notes:** Localize for CA/NY/WA wage statements, restrictive covenant limits, and pay transparency statutes.

title: Written Consent of the Board (Delaware Corporation)
description: Board written consent under DGCL §141(f) for routine corporate actions.
body:
# WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS

[COMPANY NAME], a Delaware corporation (the "Company")

The undersigned, constituting all / a majority of the directors of the Company, acting by written consent pursuant to Section 141(f) of the Delaware General Corporation Law, hereby adopt the following resolutions:

**RESOLVED**, that the Company is authorized to [ACTION], on terms substantially as presented to the Board.

**RESOLVED FURTHER**, that the officers of the Company are authorized to execute all documents and take all actions necessary or desirable to carry out the foregoing.

This consent may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature.

Dated: [DATE]

_______________________________
[Director Name]

**Drafting notes:** Confirm quorum/authorization under bylaws; attach exhibits; consider stockholder approval if required.

title: Litigation Hold Notice (US)
description: Internal litigation hold / preservation notice for anticipated or pending US litigation.
body:
# LITIGATION HOLD NOTICE

**To:** [Custodians / Departments]
**From:** Legal
**Re:** Preservation of documents — [MATTER]
**Date:** [DATE]

You must preserve all potentially relevant documents and ESI relating to [MATTER DESCRIPTION], including email, chats, drafts, calendars, and personal devices used for Company business.

**Do not** delete, alter, or auto-purge relevant materials. Suspend ordinary deletion for this matter.

**Scope.** Time period: [FROM]–[TO]. Topics: [LIST]. Custodians: [LIST].

Contact Legal at [EMAIL] with questions. Failure to preserve may result in sanctions and disciplinary action.

**Drafting notes:** Align with FRCP 37(e); issue promptly when litigation is reasonably anticipated.

title: IP Assignment & Work-for-Hire Checklist (US)
description: Checklist for securing IP assignments from employees and contractors under US law.
body:
# IP Assignment Checklist (US)

- [ ] Identify all creators (employees, contractors, consultants, interns)
- [ ] Confirm employment agreement includes present assignment of IP and moral-rights waiver where enforceable
- [ ] For contractors: signed IP assignment + work-made-for-hire language where applicable (and backup assignment)
- [ ] Check state limits on employee invention assignment (e.g., CA Lab. Code §2870)
- [ ] Collect invention disclosures for pre-existing IP and carve-outs
- [ ] Confirm open-source / third-party license compliance for inbound code
- [ ] Record assignments for patents/trademarks with USPTO where needed
- [ ] Update contractor SOWs to incorporate assignment schedules
- [ ] Privilege: route sensitive invention disclosures through counsel when appropriate

**Practical notes:** Prefer present-tense "hereby assigns" language; avoid mere agreements to assign.

title: DPIA Outline (US Org Processing EU Data)
description: Data Protection Impact Assessment outline for US organizations processing EU personal data.
body:
# DATA PROTECTION IMPACT ASSESSMENT (OUTLINE)

1. **Processing description** — purposes, categories of data subjects, personal data, recipients, retention.
2. **Necessity & proportionality** — lawful basis, minimization, alternatives considered.
3. **Risks to rights and freedoms** — likelihood/severity; special categories; automated decisions.
4. **Mitigations** — technical/organizational measures, SCCs/transfer tools, access controls.
5. **Stakeholder consultation** — DPO/privacy counsel; residual risk acceptance.
6. **Sign-off** — owner, date, review cadence.

**Drafting notes:** Not a substitute for counsel; map to GDPR Art. 35 and applicable US state privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA) where overlapping.

title: Settlement Agreement & Release (US Commercial)

body:

title: M&A Legal Diligence Checklist (US Target)
description: Buyer-side legal diligence checklist for a US corporate acquisition.
body:
# US M&A Legal Diligence Checklist

- [ ] Corporate: charter, bylaws, minute books, cap table, options/warrants
- [ ] Material contracts: change-of-control, assignment, MFNs, exclusivity
- [ ] Employment: key agreements, classification, ERISA/benefits, unions

title: Arbitration Clause (AAA Commercial, US)
description: Sample arbitration clause for US commercial contracts (AAA rules).
body:
# ARBITRATION

Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules. The seat shall be [CITY, STATE]. The language shall be English. Judgment on the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

**Exceptions.** Either party may seek provisional injunctive relief in court to protect IP or confidential information.

**Class action waiver.** Claims must be brought in an individual capacity, not as a class or representative action, to the extent permitted by law.

**Drafting notes:** Consumer/employment arbitration may require different rules and may be restricted by statute; confirm FAA applicability and state law.

title: Tax Controversy Intake Checklist (US)
description: Intake checklist for IRS/state tax controversy matters.
body:
# Tax Controversy Intake Checklist

- [ ] Identify tax years, forms, and assessing authority (IRS / state)
- [ ] Collect notices (CP2000, 30-day, 90-day, levy, lien)
- [ ] Calendar response deadlines and statutes of limitations
- [ ] Engagement letter + Form 2848 / state POA
- [ ] Gather returns, workpapers, bank statements, contracts
- [ ] Privilege: Kovel / attorney-client boundaries with accountants
- [ ] Assess penalties (accuracy, fraud, failure to file/pay) and reasonable-cause facts
